# `iced::time::SystemTime`

```rust
pub struct SystemTime(/* private fields */);
```

A measurement of the system clock, useful for talking to external entities like the file system or other processes.

Distinct from the [`Instant`](struct.Instant.md) type, this time measurement **is not monotonic**. This means that you can save a file to the file system, then save another file to the file system, **and the second file has a `SystemTime` measurement earlier than the first**. In other words, an operation that happens after another operation in real time may have an earlier `SystemTime`!

Consequently, comparing two `SystemTime` instances to learn about the duration between them returns a [`Result`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html) instead of an infallible [`Duration`](struct.Duration.md) to indicate that this sort of time drift may happen and needs to be handled.

Although a `SystemTime` cannot be directly inspected, the [`UNIX_EPOCH`](struct.SystemTime.md) constant is provided in this module as an anchor in time to learn information about a `SystemTime`. By calculating the duration from this fixed point in time, a `SystemTime` can be converted to a human-readable time, or perhaps some other string representation.

The size of a `SystemTime` struct may vary depending on the target operating system.

A `SystemTime` does not count leap seconds. `SystemTime::now()`’s behavior around a leap second is the same as the operating system’s wall clock. The precise behavior near a leap second (e.g. whether the clock appears to run slow or fast, or stop, or jump) depends on platform and configuration, so should not be relied on.

Example:

```rust
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};
use std::thread::sleep;

fn main() {
   let now = SystemTime::now();

   // we sleep for 2 seconds
   sleep(Duration::new(2, 0));
   match now.elapsed() {
       Ok(elapsed) => {
           // it prints '2'
           println!("{}", elapsed.as_secs());
       }
       Err(e) => {
           // the system clock went backwards!
           println!("Great Scott! {e:?}");
       }
   }
}
```

## Platform-specific behavior

The precision of `SystemTime` can depend on the underlying OS-specific time format. For example, on Windows the time is represented in 100 nanosecond intervals whereas Linux can represent nanosecond intervals.

The following system calls are [currently](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html#platform-specific-behavior) being used by `now()` to find out the current time:

| Platform | System call |
| --- | --- |
| SGX | [`insecure_time` usercall](https://edp.fortanix.com/docs/api/fortanix_sgx_abi/struct.Usercalls.html#method.insecure_time). More information on [timekeeping in SGX](https://edp.fortanix.com/docs/concepts/rust-std/#codestdtimecode) |
| UNIX | [clock_gettime (Realtime Clock)](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/clock_getres.html) |
| Darwin | [clock_gettime (Realtime Clock)](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/clock_getres.html) |
| VXWorks | [clock_gettime (Realtime Clock)](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/clock_getres.html) |
| SOLID | `SOLID_RTC_ReadTime` |
| WASI | [__wasi_clock_time_get (Realtime Clock)](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI/blob/main/legacy/preview1/docs.md#clock_time_get) |
| Windows | [GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsystemtimepreciseasfiletime) / [GetSystemTimeAsFileTime](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsystemtimeasfiletime) |

**Disclaimer:** These system calls might change over time.

> Note: mathematical operations like [`add`](struct.SystemTime.md) may panic if the underlying structure cannot represent the new point in time.

**Source:** [time.rs.html#250](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/std/time.rs.html#250) (lines 250)

## Methods

### `impl SystemTime`

#### `UNIX_EPOCH`

```rust
pub const UNIX_EPOCH: SystemTime = UNIX_EPOCH
```

An anchor in time which can be used to create new `SystemTime` instances or learn about where in time a `SystemTime` lies.

This constant is defined to be “1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC” on all systems with respect to the system clock. Using `duration_since` on an existing `SystemTime` instance can tell how far away from this point in time a measurement lies, and using `UNIX_EPOCH + duration` can be used to create a `SystemTime` instance to represent another fixed point in time.

`duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs()` returns the number of non-leap seconds since the start of 1970 UTC. This is a POSIX `time_t` (as a `u64`), and is the same time representation as used in many Internet protocols.

###### Examples

```rust
use std::time::SystemTime;

match SystemTime::now().duration_since(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH) {
    Ok(n) => println!("1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC was {} seconds ago!", n.as_secs()),
    Err(_) => panic!("SystemTime before UNIX EPOCH!"),
}
```

#### `MAX`

```rust
pub const MAX: SystemTime
```

*🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (time_systemtime_limits)*

Represents the maximum value representable by [`SystemTime`](struct.SystemTime.md) on this platform.

This value differs a lot between platforms, but it is always the case that any positive addition of a [`Duration`](struct.Duration.md), whose value is greater than or equal to the time precision of the operating system, to [`SystemTime::MAX`](struct.SystemTime.md) will fail.

###### Examples

```rust
#![feature(time_systemtime_limits)]
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

// Adding zero will change nothing.
assert_eq!(SystemTime::MAX.checked_add(Duration::ZERO), Some(SystemTime::MAX));

// But adding just one second will already fail ...
//
// Keep in mind that this in fact may succeed, if the Duration is
// smaller than the time precision of the operating system, which
// happens to be 1ns on most operating systems, with Windows being the
// notable exception by using 100ns, hence why this example uses 1s.
assert_eq!(SystemTime::MAX.checked_add(Duration::new(1, 0)), None);

// Utilize this for saturating arithmetic to improve error handling.
// In this case, we will use a certificate with a timestamp in the
// future as a practical example.
let configured_offset = Duration::from_secs(60 * 60 * 24);
let valid_after =
    SystemTime::now()
        .checked_add(configured_offset)
        .unwrap_or(SystemTime::MAX);
```

#### `MIN`

```rust
pub const MIN: SystemTime
```

*🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (time_systemtime_limits)*

Represents the minimum value representable by [`SystemTime`](struct.SystemTime.md) on this platform.

This value differs a lot between platforms, but it is always the case that any positive subtraction of a [`Duration`](struct.Duration.md) from, whose value is greater than or equal to the time precision of the operating system, to [`SystemTime::MIN`](struct.SystemTime.md) will fail.

Depending on the platform, this may be either less than or equal to [`SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH`](struct.SystemTime.md), depending on whether the operating system supports the representation of timestamps before the Unix epoch or not. However, it is always guaranteed that a [`SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH`](struct.SystemTime.md) fits between a [`SystemTime::MIN`](struct.SystemTime.md) and [`SystemTime::MAX`](struct.SystemTime.md).

###### Examples

```rust
#![feature(time_systemtime_limits)]
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

// Subtracting zero will change nothing.
assert_eq!(SystemTime::MIN.checked_sub(Duration::ZERO), Some(SystemTime::MIN));

// But subtracting just one second will already fail.
//
// Keep in mind that this in fact may succeed, if the Duration is
// smaller than the time precision of the operating system, which
// happens to be 1ns on most operating systems, with Windows being the
// notable exception by using 100ns, hence why this example uses 1s.
assert_eq!(SystemTime::MIN.checked_sub(Duration::new(1, 0)), None);

// Utilize this for saturating arithmetic to improve error handling.
// In this case, we will use a cache expiry as a practical example.
let configured_expiry = Duration::from_secs(60 * 3);
let expiry_threshold =
    SystemTime::now()
        .checked_sub(configured_expiry)
        .unwrap_or(SystemTime::MIN);
```

#### `now`

```rust
pub fn now() -> SystemTime
```

Returns the system time corresponding to “now”.

###### Examples

```rust
use std::time::SystemTime;

let sys_time = SystemTime::now();
```

#### `duration_since`

```rust
pub fn duration_since( &self, earlier: SystemTime, ) -> Result<Duration, SystemTimeError>
```

Returns the amount of time elapsed from an earlier point in time.

This function may fail because measurements taken earlier are not guaranteed to always be before later measurements (due to anomalies such as the system clock being adjusted either forwards or backwards). [`Instant`](struct.Instant.md) can be used to measure elapsed time without this risk of failure.

If successful, `Ok(Duration)` is returned where the duration represents the amount of time elapsed from the specified measurement to this one.

Returns an [`Err`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err) if `earlier` is later than `self`, and the error contains how far from `self` the time is.

###### Examples

```rust
use std::time::SystemTime;

let sys_time = SystemTime::now();
let new_sys_time = SystemTime::now();
let difference = new_sys_time.duration_since(sys_time)
    .expect("Clock may have gone backwards");
println!("{difference:?}");
```

#### `elapsed`

```rust
pub fn elapsed(&self) -> Result<Duration, SystemTimeError>
```

Returns the difference from this system time to the current clock time.

This function may fail as the underlying system clock is susceptible to drift and updates (e.g., the system clock could go backwards), so this function might not always succeed. If successful, `Ok(Duration)` is returned where the duration represents the amount of time elapsed from this time measurement to the current time.

To measure elapsed time reliably, use [`Instant`](struct.Instant.md) instead.

Returns an [`Err`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err) if `self` is later than the current system time, and the error contains how far from the current system time `self` is.

###### Examples

```rust
use std::thread::sleep;
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

let sys_time = SystemTime::now();
let one_sec = Duration::from_secs(1);
sleep(one_sec);
assert!(sys_time.elapsed().unwrap() >= one_sec);
```

#### `checked_add`

```rust
pub fn checked_add(&self, duration: Duration) -> Option<SystemTime>
```

Returns `Some(t)` where `t` is the time `self + duration` if `t` can be represented as `SystemTime` (which means it’s inside the bounds of the underlying data structure), `None` otherwise.

In the case that the `duration` is smaller than the time precision of the operating system, `Some(self)` will be returned.

#### `checked_sub`

```rust
pub fn checked_sub(&self, duration: Duration) -> Option<SystemTime>
```

Returns `Some(t)` where `t` is the time `self - duration` if `t` can be represented as `SystemTime` (which means it’s inside the bounds of the underlying data structure), `None` otherwise.

In the case that the `duration` is smaller than the time precision of the operating system, `Some(self)` will be returned.

#### `saturating_add`

```rust
pub fn saturating_add(&self, duration: Duration) -> SystemTime
```

*🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (time_saturating_systemtime)*

Saturating [`SystemTime`](struct.SystemTime.md) addition, computing `self + duration`, returning [`SystemTime::MAX`](struct.SystemTime.md) if overflow occurred.

In the case that the `duration` is smaller than the time precision of the operating system, `self` will be returned.

#### `saturating_sub`

```rust
pub fn saturating_sub(&self, duration: Duration) -> SystemTime
```

*🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (time_saturating_systemtime)*

Saturating [`SystemTime`](struct.SystemTime.md) subtraction, computing `self - duration`, returning [`SystemTime::MIN`](struct.SystemTime.md) if overflow occurred.

In the case that the `duration` is smaller than the time precision of the operating system, `self` will be returned.

#### `saturating_duration_since`

```rust
pub fn saturating_duration_since(&self, earlier: SystemTime) -> Duration
```

*🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (time_saturating_systemtime)*

Saturating computation of time elapsed from an earlier point in time, returning [`Duration::ZERO`](struct.Duration.md) in the case that `earlier` is later or equal to `self`.

###### Examples

```rust
#![feature(time_saturating_systemtime)]
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

let now = SystemTime::now();
let prev = now.saturating_sub(Duration::new(1, 0));

// now - prev should return non-zero.
assert_eq!(now.saturating_duration_since(prev), Duration::new(1, 0));
assert!(now.duration_since(prev).is_ok());

// prev - now should return zero (and fail with the non-saturating).
assert_eq!(prev.saturating_duration_since(now), Duration::ZERO);
assert!(prev.duration_since(now).is_err());

// now - now should return zero (and work with the non-saturating).
assert_eq!(now.saturating_duration_since(now), Duration::ZERO);
assert!(now.duration_since(now).is_ok());
```

# `iced::widget::component`

```rust
pub fn component<'a, C, Message, Theme, Renderer>(
    component: C,
) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'awhere
    C: Component<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a,
    <C as Component<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer>>::State: 'static,
    Message: 'a,
    Theme: 'a,
```

# `iced::widget::markdown`

```rust
pub fn markdown<'a, Theme, Renderer>(
    items: &'a [Item],
    settings: impl Into<Settings>,
    theme: Theme,
) -> impl Widget<String, Theme, Renderer> + 'awhere
    Theme: Catalog + 'static,
    Renderer: Renderer,
```

Display a bunch of Markdown items.

You can obtain the items with [`parse`](markdown/fn.parse.md).

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::markdown;
use iced::{Theme, Widget};

struct State {
   markdown: Vec<markdown::Item>,
}

enum Message {
    LinkClicked(markdown::Uri),
}

impl State {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            markdown: markdown::parse("This is some **Markdown**!").collect(),
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message> {
        markdown::view(
            &self.markdown,
            markdown::Settings::default(),
            Theme::TokyoNight,
        )
            .map(Message::LinkClicked)
    }

    fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::LinkClicked(url) => {
                println!("The following url was clicked: {url}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# `iced::widget::transition`

```rust
pub fn transition<'a, Message, W, P>(
    value: <P as Program>::Value,
    init: impl Fn() -> P + 'a,
    view: impl Fn(&P, Instant) -> W + 'a,
) -> Transition<'a, Message, W, P> where
    P: Program,
```

Creates a new [`Transition`](transition/struct.Transition.md).

The `init` closure will be used to initialize an implementor of [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md). This is normally an [`Animation`](../struct.Animation.md), but you can implement [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md) on your own types as well.

The `view` closure will receive the [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md) and the current [`Instant`](../time/struct.Instant.md), which can be used for interpolating values. When the `value` changes, this will be called every frame, until the [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md) stops animating.

## Example

Here is how you could implement a smooth progress bar:

```rust
use iced::widget::{transition, progress_bar};
use iced::Animation;

fn smooth_progress_bar<Message>(progress: f32) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    transition(progress, || Animation::new(0.).quick(), |animation, now| {
        progress_bar(0.0..=1.0, animation.interpolate_with(std::convert::identity, now))
    })
}
```

**Source:** [helpers.rs](../../src/iced_widget/helpers.rs.md) (lines 1769-1775)

# `iced::widget`

Use the built-in widgets or create your own.

## Modules

- [`button`](button/index.md) — Buttons allow your users to perform actions by pressing them.
- [`canvas`](canvas/index.md) *(canvas)* — Canvases can be leveraged to draw interactive 2D graphics.
- [`checkbox`](checkbox/index.md) — Checkboxes can be used to let users make binary choices.
- [`combo_box`](combo_box/index.md) — Combo boxes display a dropdown list of searchable and selectable options.
- [`component`](component/index.md) — Build and reuse custom widgets using The Elm Architecture.
- [`container`](container/index.md) — Containers let you align a widget inside their boundaries.
- [`float`](float/index.md) — Make elements float!
- [`grid`](grid/index.md) — Distribute content on a grid.
- [`image`](image/index.md) *(image-without-codecs)* — Images display raster graphics in different formats (PNG, JPG, etc.).
- [`keyed`](keyed/index.md) — Keyed widgets can provide hints to ensure continuity.
- [`lazy`](lazy/index.md) — A widget that only rebuilds its contents when necessary.
- [`markdown`](markdown/index.md) *(markdown)* — Markdown widgets can parse and display Markdown.
- [`operation`](operation/index.md) — Change internal widget state.
- [`overlay`](overlay/index.md) — Display interactive elements on top of other widgets.
- [`pane_grid`](pane_grid/index.md) — Pane grids let your users split regions of your application and organize layout dynamically.
- [`pick_list`](pick_list/index.md) — Pick lists display a dropdown list of selectable options.
- [`progress_bar`](progress_bar/index.md) — Progress bars visualize the progression of an extended computer operation, such as a download, file transfer, or installation.
- [`qr_code`](qr_code/index.md) *(qr_code)* — QR codes display information in a type of two-dimensional matrix barcode.
- [`radio`](radio/index.md) — Radio buttons let users choose a single option from a bunch of options.
- [`row`](row/index.md) — Distribute content horizontally.
- [`rule`](rule/index.md) — Rules divide space horizontally or vertically.
- [`scrollable`](scrollable/index.md) — Scrollables let users navigate an endless amount of content with a scrollbar.
- [`selector`](selector/index.md) *(selector)* — Find and query widgets in your applications.
- [`sensor`](sensor/index.md) — Generate messages when content pops in and out of view.
- [`shader`](shader/index.md) *(wgpu)* — A custom shader widget for wgpu applications.
- [`slider`](slider/index.md) — Sliders let users set a value by moving an indicator.
- [`space`](space/index.md) — Add some explicit spacing between elements.
- [`sticky`](sticky/index.md) — Stick elements to the viewport!
- [`svg`](svg/index.md) *(svg)* — Svg widgets display vector graphics in your application.
- [`table`](table/index.md) — Display tables.
- [`text`](text/index.md) — Draw and interact with text.
- [`text_editor`](text_editor/index.md) — Text editors display a multi-line text input for text editing.
- [`text_input`](text_input/index.md) — Text inputs display fields that can be filled with text.
- [`theme`](theme/index.md) — Use the built-in theme and styles.
- [`toggler`](toggler/index.md) — Togglers let users make binary choices by toggling a switch.
- [`tooltip`](tooltip/index.md) — Tooltips display a hint of information over some element when hovered.
- [`transition`](transition/index.md) — A widget to make animated views.
- [`vertical_slider`](vertical_slider/index.md) — Sliders let users set a value by moving an indicator.

# `iced::widget::column`

```rust
macro_rules! column {
    () => { ... };
    ($($x:expr),+ $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```

Creates a [`Column`](struct.Column.md) with the given children.

Columns distribute their children vertically.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{button, column};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    column![
        "I am on top!",
        button("I am in the center!"),
        "I am below.",
    ]
}
```

# `iced::widget::Button`

```rust
pub struct Button<'a, Message, W = Element<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>>, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A generic widget that produces a message when pressed.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::button;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    ButtonPressed,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    button("Press me!").on_press(Message::ButtonPressed)
}
```

If a [`Button::on_press`](struct.Button.md) handler is not set, the resulting [`Button`](struct.Button.md) will be disabled:

```rust
use iced::widget::button;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    ButtonPressed,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    button("I am disabled!")
}
```

**Source:** [button.rs](../../src/iced_widget/button.rs.md) (lines 71)

#### `on_press_with`

```rust
pub fn on_press_with( self, on_press: impl Fn() -> Message + 'a, ) -> Button<'a, Message, W, Theme>
```

Sets the message that will be produced when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is pressed.

This is analogous to [`Button::on_press`](struct.Button.md), but using a closure to produce the message.

This closure will only be called when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is actually pressed and, therefore, this method is useful to reduce overhead if creating the resulting message is slow.

#### `on_press_maybe_with`

Sets the message that will be produced when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is pressed, if `Some`.

This is analogous to [`Button::on_press`](struct.Button.md), but using a closure to produce the message.

This closure will only be called when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is actually pressed and, therefore, this method is useful to reduce overhead if creating the resulting message is slow.

# `iced::widget::Canvas`

```rust
pub struct Canvas<P, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Renderer: Renderer,
    P: Program<Message, Theme, Renderer>, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget capable of drawing 2D graphics.

## Example: Drawing a Simple Circle

```rust
use iced::mouse;
use iced::widget::canvas;
use iced::{Color, Rectangle, Renderer, Theme};

// First, we define the data we need for drawing
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Circle {
    radius: f32,
}

// Then, we implement the `Program` trait
impl<Message> canvas::Program<Message> for Circle {
    // No internal state
    type State = ();

    fn draw(
        &self,
        _state: &(),
        renderer: &Renderer,
        _theme: &Theme,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: mouse::Cursor
    ) -> Vec<canvas::Geometry> {
        // We prepare a new `Frame`
        let mut frame = canvas::Frame::new(renderer, bounds.size());

        // We create a `Path` representing a simple circle
        let circle = canvas::Path::circle(frame.center(), self.radius);

        // And fill it with some color
        frame.fill(&circle, Color::BLACK);

        // Then, we produce the geometry
        vec![frame.into_geometry()]
    }
}

// Finally, we simply use our `Circle` to create the `Canvas`!
fn view<Message>(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    canvas(Circle { radius: 50.0 })
}
```

**Source:** [canvas.rs](../../src/iced_widget/canvas.rs.md) (lines 138)

# `iced::widget::Checkbox`

```rust
pub struct Checkbox<'a, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Theme: Catalog,
    Renderer: Renderer, { /* private fields */ }
```

A box that can be checked.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::checkbox;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    CheckboxToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    checkbox(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::CheckboxToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::CheckboxToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

![Checkbox drawn by iced_wgpu](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced/blob/7760618fb112074bc40b148944521f312152012a/docs/images/checkbox.png?raw=true)

**Source:** [checkbox.rs](../../src/iced_widget/checkbox.rs.md) (lines 82)

```rust

```

Sets the function that will be called when the [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) is toggled. It will receive the new state of the [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) and must produce a `Message`.

Unless `on_toggle` is called, the [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) will be disabled.

#### `on_toggle_maybe`

If `None`, the checkbox will be disabled.

# `iced::widget::Column`

```rust
pub struct Column<W> { /* private fields */ }
```

A container that distributes its contents vertically.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{button, column};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    column![
        "I am on top!",
        button("I am in the center!"),
        "I am below.",
    ]
}
```

# `iced::widget::ComboBox`

```rust
pub struct ComboBox<'a, T, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget for searching and selecting a single value from a list of options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::combo_box;

struct State {
   fruits: combo_box::State<Fruit>,
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    combo_box(
        &state.fruits,
        "Select your favorite fruit...",
        state.favorite.as_ref(),
        Message::FruitSelected
    )
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

**Source:** [combo_box.rs](../../src/iced_widget/combo_box.rs.md) (lines 131)

# `iced::widget::Container`

```rust
pub struct Container<'a, W, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that aligns its contents inside of its boundaries.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::container;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    container("This text is centered inside a rounded box!")
        .padding(10)
        .center(800)
        .style(container::rounded_box)
}
```

**Source:** [container.rs](../../src/iced_widget/container.rs.md) (lines 56)

# `iced::widget::Hover`

```rust
pub struct Hover<W, V> { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that displays another widget on top of it.

This works analogously to a [`stack`](struct.Stack.md), but it will only display the layer on top when the cursor is over the base. It can be useful for removing visual clutter.

**Source:** [hover.rs](../../src/iced_widget/hover.rs.md) (lines 20)

## Methods

# `iced::widget::Image`

```rust
pub struct Image<Handle = Handle> { /* private fields */ }
```

A frame that displays an image while keeping aspect ratio.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::image;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    image("ferris.png")
}
```

![](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced/blob/9712b319bb7a32848001b96bd84977430f14b623/examples/resources/ferris.png?raw=true)

**Source:** [image.rs](../../src/iced_widget/image.rs.md) (lines 55)

## Methods

### `impl<Handle> Image<Handle>`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(handle: impl Into<Handle>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Creates a new [`Image`](struct.Image.md) with the given path.

#### `width`

```rust
pub fn width(self, width: impl Into<Length>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the width of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md) boundaries.

#### `height`

```rust
pub fn height(self, height: impl Into<Length>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the height of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md) boundaries.

#### `expand`

```rust
pub fn expand(self, expand: bool) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets whether the [`Image`](struct.Image.md) should try to fill as much space available as possible while keeping aspect ratio and without allocating extra space in any axis with a [`Length::Shrink`](../enum.Length.md) sizing strategy.

This is similar to using [`Length::Fill`](../enum.Length.md) for both the [`width`](struct.Image.md) and the [`height`](struct.Image.md), but without the downside of blank space.

#### `content_fit`

```rust
pub fn content_fit(self, content_fit: ContentFit) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the [`ContentFit`](../enum.ContentFit.md) of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

Defaults to [`ContentFit::Contain`](../enum.ContentFit.md)

#### `filter_method`

```rust
pub fn filter_method(self, filter_method: FilterMethod) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the [`FilterMethod`](../advanced/image/enum.FilterMethod.md) of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

#### `rotation`

```rust
pub fn rotation(self, rotation: impl Into<Rotation>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Applies the given [`Rotation`](../enum.Rotation.md) to the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

#### `opacity`

```rust
pub fn opacity(self, opacity: impl Into<f32>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the opacity of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

It should be in the [0.0, 1.0] range—`0.0` meaning completely transparent, and `1.0` meaning completely opaque.

#### `scale`

```rust
pub fn scale(self, scale: impl Into<f32>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the scale of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

The region of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md) drawn will be scaled from the center by the given scale factor. This can be useful to create certain effects and animations, like smooth zoom in / out.

#### `crop`

```rust
pub fn crop(self, region: Rectangle<u32>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Crops the [`Image`](struct.Image.md) to the given region described by the [`Rectangle`](../struct.Rectangle.md) in absolute coordinates.

Cropping is done before applying any transformation or [`ContentFit`](../enum.ContentFit.md). In practice, this means that cropping an [`Image`](struct.Image.md) with this method should produce the same result as cropping it externally (e.g. with an image editor) and creating a new [`Handle`](../advanced/image/enum.Handle.md) for the cropped version.

However, this method is much more efficient; since it just leverages scissoring during rendering and no image cropping actually takes place. Instead, it reuses the existing image allocations and should be as efficient as not cropping at all!

The `region` coordinates will be clamped to the image dimensions, if necessary.

#### `border_radius`

```rust
pub fn border_radius(self, border_radius: impl Into<Radius>) -> Image<Handle>
```

*Available on crate feature image-without-codecs only.*

Sets the [`border::Radius`](../border/struct.Radius.md) of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

Currently, it will only be applied around the rectangular bounding box of the [`Image`](struct.Image.md).

Emit messages on mouse events.

**Source:** [mouse_area.rs](../../src/iced_widget/mouse_area.rs.md) (lines 11)

## Methods

### `impl<'a, Message, W> MouseArea<'a, Message, W>`

#### `on_press`

```rust

```

The message to emit on a left button press.

#### `on_release`

```rust
pub fn on_release(self, message: Message) -> MouseArea<'a, Message, W>
```

The message to emit on a left button release.

#### `on_double_click`

```rust
pub fn on_double_click(self, message: Message) -> MouseArea<'a, Message, W>
```

The message to emit on a double click.

If you use this with [`on_press`](struct.MouseArea.md)/[`on_release`](struct.MouseArea.md), those event will be emit as normal.

The events stream will be: on_press -> on_release -> on_press -> on_double_click -> on_release -> on_press …

# `iced::widget::PaneGrid`

```rust
pub struct PaneGrid<'a, Message, T, W, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Theme: Catalog,
    Renderer: Renderer, { /* private fields */ }
```

A collection of panes distributed using either vertical or horizontal splits to completely fill the space available.

![Pane grid - Iced](https://iced.rs/examples/pane_grid.gif)

This distribution of space is common in tiling window managers (like [`awesome`](https://awesomewm.org/), [`i3`](https://i3wm.org/), or even [`tmux`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux)).

A [`PaneGrid`](struct.PaneGrid.md) supports:

- Vertical and horizontal splits
- Tracking of the last active pane
- Mouse-based resizing
- Drag and drop to reorganize panes
- Hotkey support
- Configurable modifier keys
- [`State`](pane_grid/struct.State.md) API to perform actions programmatically (`split`, `swap`, `resize`, etc.)

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{pane_grid, text};

struct State {
    panes: pane_grid::State<Pane>,
}

enum Pane {
    SomePane,
    AnotherKindOfPane,
}

enum Message {
    PaneDragged(pane_grid::DragEvent),
    PaneResized(pane_grid::ResizeEvent),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    pane_grid(&state.panes, |pane, state, is_maximized| {
        pane_grid::Content::new(match state {
            Pane::SomePane => text("This is some pane"),
            Pane::AnotherKindOfPane => text("This is another kind of pane"),
        })
    })
    .on_drag(Message::PaneDragged)
    .on_resize(10, Message::PaneResized)
}
```

**Source:** [pane_grid.rs](../../src/iced_widget/pane_grid.rs.md) (lines 148)

#### `on_resize`

```rust
pub fn on_resize<F>( self, leeway: impl Into<Pixels>, f: F, ) -> PaneGrid<'a, Message, T, W, Theme, Renderer> where F: 'a + Fn(ResizeEvent) -> Message,
```

Enables the resize interactions of the [`PaneGrid`](struct.PaneGrid.md), which will use the provided function to produce messages.

The `leeway` describes the amount of space around a split that can be used to grab it.

The grabbable area of a split will have a length of `spacing + leeway`, properly centered. In other words, a length of `(spacing + leeway) / 2.0` on either side of the split line.

# `iced::widget::PickList`

```rust
pub struct PickList<'a, T, L, V, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    T: PartialEq + Clone,
    L: Borrow<[T]> + 'a,
    V: Borrow<T> + 'a,
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget for selecting a single value from a list of options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::pick_list;

struct State {
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let fruits = [
        Fruit::Apple,
        Fruit::Orange,
        Fruit::Strawberry,
        Fruit::Tomato,
    ];

    pick_list(
        state.favorite,
        fruits,
        Fruit::to_string,
    )
    .on_select(Message::FruitSelected)
    .placeholder("Select your favorite fruit...")
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

**Source:** [pick_list.rs](../../src/iced_widget/pick_list.rs.md) (lines 146)

# `iced::widget::Pin`

```rust
pub struct Pin<W> { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that positions its contents at some fixed coordinates inside of its boundaries.

By default, a [`Pin`](struct.Pin.md) widget will try to fill its parent.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::pin;
use iced::Fill;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    pin("This text is displayed at coordinates (50, 50)!")
        .x(50)
        .y(50)
}
```

**Source:** [pin.rs](../../src/iced_widget/pin.rs.md) (lines 52)

# `iced::widget::ProgressBar`

```rust
pub struct ProgressBar<'a, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A bar that displays progress.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::progress_bar;

struct State {
   progress: f32,
}

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    progress_bar(0.0..=100.0, state.progress)
}
```

# `iced::widget::QRCode`

```rust
pub struct QRCode<'a, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A type of matrix barcode consisting of squares arranged in a grid which can be read by an imaging device, such as a camera.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::qr_code;

struct State {
   data: qr_code::Data,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    qr_code(&state.data)
}
```

**Source:** [qr_code.rs](../../src/iced_widget/qr_code.rs.md) (lines 61)

## Methods

# `iced::widget::Radio`

```rust
pub struct Radio<'a, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A circular button representing a choice.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{column, radio};

struct State {
   selection: Option<Choice>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum Message {
    RadioSelected(Choice),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Choice {
    A,
    B,
    C,
    All,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let a = radio(
        "A",
        Choice::A,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let b = radio(
        "B",
        Choice::B,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let c = radio(
        "C",
        Choice::C,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let all = radio(
        "All of the above",
        Choice::All,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected
    );

    column![a, b, c, all]
}
```

**Source:** [radio.rs](../../src/iced_widget/radio.rs.md) (lines 131)

# `iced::widget::Responsive`

```rust
pub struct Responsive<'a, W> { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that is aware of its dimensions.

A [`Responsive`](struct.Responsive.md) widget will always try to fill all the available space of its parent.

**Source:** [responsive.rs](../../src/iced_widget/responsive.rs.md) (lines 13)

## Methods

### `impl<'a, W> Responsive<'a, W>`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(view: impl Fn(Size) -> W + 'a) -> Responsive<'a, W>
```

Creates a new [`Responsive`](struct.Responsive.md) widget with a closure that produces its contents.

The `view` closure will receive the maximum available space for the [`Responsive`](struct.Responsive.md) during layout. You can use this [`Size`](../struct.Size.md) to conditionally build the contents.

# `iced::widget::Row`

```rust
pub struct Row<W> { /* private fields */ }
```

A container that distributes its contents horizontally.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{button, row};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    row![
        "I am to the left!",
        button("I am in the middle!"),
        "I am to the right!",
    ]
}
```

**Source:** [row.rs](../../src/iced_widget/row.rs.md) (lines 32)

## Methods

### `impl<W> Row<W>`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new() -> Row<W>
```

Creates an empty [`Row`](struct.Row.md).

#### `with_capacity`

```rust
pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Row<W>
```

Creates a [`Row`](struct.Row.md) with the given capacity.

#### `with_children`

```rust
pub fn with_children(children: impl IntoIterator<Item = W>) -> Row<W> where W: Meta,
```

Creates a [`Row`](struct.Row.md) with the given widgets.

#### `from_vec`

```rust
pub fn from_vec(children: Vec<W>) -> Row<W>
```

Creates a [`Row`](struct.Row.md) from an already allocated [`Vec`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html).

Keep in mind that the [`Row`](struct.Row.md) will not inspect the [`Vec`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html), which means it won’t automatically adapt to the sizing strategy of its contents.

If any of the children have a [`Length::Fill`](../enum.Length.md) strategy, you will need to call [`Row::width`](struct.Row.md) or [`Row::height`](struct.Row.md) accordingly.

#### `spacing`

```rust
pub fn spacing(self, amount: impl Into<Pixels>) -> Row<W>
```

Sets the horizontal spacing *between* elements.

Custom margins per element do not exist in iced. You should use this method instead! While less flexible, it helps you keep spacing between elements consistent.

# `iced::widget::Rule`

```rust
pub struct Rule<'a, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

Display a horizontal or vertical rule for dividing content.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::rule;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    // ...,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    rule::horizontal(2)
}
```

**Source:** [rule.rs](../../src/iced_widget/rule.rs.md) (lines 69)

# `iced::widget::Scrollable`

```rust
pub struct Scrollable<'a, Message, W = Element<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>>, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that can vertically display an infinite amount of content with a scrollbar.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{column, scrollable, space};

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    scrollable(column![
        "Scroll me!",
        space().height(3000),
        "You did it!",
    ])
}
```

## Scrollbars

A scrollbar has two interactive parts: the *scroller* (the draggable thumb) and the *rail* (the track it slides on).

- Pressing and dragging the **scroller** moves it 1:1 with the pointer.
- Pressing the **rail** scrolls one page (animated like a wheel scroll when [`Self::smooth_scroll`](struct.Scrollable.md) is enabled). While the button is held, the scroller then slides toward the pointer at a constant speed, stopping when its edge reaches the pointer; moving the pointer moves the target with it. This mirrors the track autoscroll of most toolkits.
- `Shift`-clicking the **rail** instead jumps the scroller so that its center is under the pointer, and then drags it from there.

With [`Self::click_to_scroll`](struct.Scrollable.md) enabled, the behavior of the rail press and the `Shift`-click is inverted.

**Source:** [scrollable.rs](../../src/iced_widget/scrollable.rs.md) (lines 83)

By default, it is disabled.

#### `smooth_scroll`

```rust
pub fn smooth_scroll( self, smooth_scroll: bool, ) -> Scrollable<'a, Message, W, Theme>
```

Sets whether wheel scrolling should be smoothed out over time, instead of moving the [`Scrollable`](struct.Scrollable.md) immediately.

When enabled, discrete scrolls (e.g. from a mouse wheel) move a target scroll offset — carrying the momentum of the wheel notches — and the [`Scrollable`](struct.Scrollable.md) eases towards it over a few frames. High-precision scrolls (e.g. from a touchpad), which are already smooth, are always applied immediately.

The setting also acts as the default behavior of the scroll operations (`snap_to`, `scroll_to`, `scroll_by`): operations with [`Animation::Auto`](operation/enum.Animation.md) scroll smoothly if and only if it is enabled.

By default, it is enabled.

#### `click_to_scroll`

```rust
pub fn click_to_scroll( self, click_to_scroll: bool, ) -> Scrollable<'a, Message, W, Theme>
```

Sets whether a plain click on the scrollbar rail should jump the scroller to the click position, instead of scrolling one page.

By default, a press on the rail scrolls one page (and autoscrolls while the button is held), while a `Shift`-click jumps the scroller so that its center is under the pointer and drags it from there.

When enabled, the behavior is inverted: a plain click jumps the scroller so that its center is under the pointer (and drags it from there), while a `Shift`-click scrolls one page (and autoscrolls while the button is held).

By default, it is disabled.

# `iced::widget::Sensor`

```rust
pub struct Sensor<'a, Key, Message, W = Element<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>>> { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that can generate messages when its content pops in and out of view.

It can even notify you with anticipation at a given distance!

**Source:** [sensor.rs](../../src/iced_widget/sensor.rs.md) (lines 15)

## Methods

### `impl<'a, Key, Message, W> Sensor<'a, Key, Message, W> where Key: Key,`

#### `on_resize`


Sets the message to be produced when the content changes [`Size`](../struct.Size.md) once its in view.

The closure will receive the new [`Size`](../struct.Size.md) of the content.

#### `on_hide`

```rust
pub fn on_hide(self, on_hide: Message) -> Sensor<'a, Key, Message, W>
```

Sets the message to be produced when the content pops out of view.

#### `key`

```rust
pub fn key<K>(self, key: K) -> Sensor<'a, impl Key, Message, W> where K: Clone + PartialEq + 'static,
```

Sets the key of the [`Sensor`](struct.Sensor.md) widget, for continuity.

If the key changes, the [`Sensor`](struct.Sensor.md) widget will trigger again.

#### `key_ref`

```rust
pub fn key_ref<K>(self, key: &'a K) -> Sensor<'a, &'a K, Message, W> where K: ToOwned + PartialEq<<K as ToOwned>::Owned> + ?Sized, <K as ToOwned>::Owned: 'static,
```

Sets the key of the [`Sensor`](struct.Sensor.md), for continuity; using a reference.

If the key changes, the [`Sensor`](struct.Sensor.md) will trigger again.

#### `anticipate`

```rust
pub fn anticipate( self, distance: impl Into<Pixels>, ) -> Sensor<'a, Key, Message, W>
```

Sets the distance in [`Pixels`](../struct.Pixels.md) to use in anticipation of the content popping into view.

This can be quite useful to lazily load items in a long scrollable behind the scenes before the user can notice it!

#### `delay`

```rust
pub fn delay(self, delay: impl Into<Duration>) -> Sensor<'a, Key, Message, W>
```

Sets the amount of time to wait before firing an [`on_show`](struct.Sensor.md) or [`on_hide`](struct.Sensor.md) event; after the content is shown or hidden.

When combined with [`key`](struct.Sensor.md), this can be useful to debounce key changes.

# `iced::widget::Shader`

```rust
pub struct Shader<Message, P> where
    P: Program<Message>, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget which can render custom shaders with Iced’s `wgpu` backend.

Must be initialized with a [`Program`](shader/trait.Program.md), which describes the internal widget state & how its [`Program::Primitive`](shader/trait.Program.md)s are drawn.

**Source:** [shader.rs](../../src/iced_widget/shader.rs.md) (lines 25)

# `iced::widget::Slider`

```rust
pub struct Slider<'a, T, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

An horizontal bar and a handle that selects a single value from a range of values.

A [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md) will try to fill the horizontal space of its container.

The [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md) range of numeric values is generic and its step size defaults to 1 unit.

Note: Under the hood values are converted to/from f64 so only values representable exactly as an f64 are possible to select via the slider. However it is likely that the precision of the slider at these scales is already less than the precision lost from the f64 representation.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::slider;

struct State {
   value: f32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    ValueChanged(f32),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    slider(0.0..=100.0, state.value, Message::ValueChanged)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::ValueChanged(value) => {
            state.value = value;
        }
    }
}
```

**Source:** [slider.rs](../../src/iced_widget/slider.rs.md) (lines 88)


#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new<F>( range: RangeInclusive<T>, value: T, on_change: F, ) -> Slider<'a, T, Message, Theme> where F: 'a + Fn(T) -> Message,
```

Creates a new [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md).

It expects:

- an inclusive range of possible values
- the current value of the [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md)
- a function that will be called when the [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md) is dragged. It receives the new value of the [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md) and must produce a `Message`.

#### `default`

```rust
pub fn default(self, default: impl Into<T>) -> Slider<'a, T, Message, Theme>
```

Sets the optional default value for the [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md).

If set, the [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md) will reset to this value when ctrl-clicked or command-clicked.

#### `on_release`

```rust
pub fn on_release(self, on_release: Message) -> Slider<'a, T, Message, Theme>
```

Sets the release message of the [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md). This is called when the mouse is released from the slider.

Typically, the user’s interaction with the slider is finished when this message is produced. This is useful if you need to spawn a long-running task from the slider’s result, where the default on_change message could create too many events.

#### `width`

# `iced::widget::Stack`

```rust
pub struct Stack<W> { /* private fields */ }
```

A container that displays children on top of each other.

The first [`Widget`](../advanced/trait.Widget.md) dictates the intrinsic [`Size`](../struct.Size.md) of a [`Stack`](struct.Stack.md) and will be displayed as the base layer. Every consecutive [`Widget`](../advanced/trait.Widget.md) will be rendered on top; on its own layer.

You can use [`push_under`](struct.Stack.md) to push a [`Widget`](../advanced/trait.Widget.md) under the current [`Stack`](struct.Stack.md) without affecting its intrinsic [`Size`](../struct.Size.md).

Keep in mind that too much layering will normally produce bad UX as well as introduce certain rendering overhead. Use this widget sparingly!

**Source:** [stack.rs](../../src/iced_widget/stack.rs.md) (lines 20)

# `iced::widget::Sticky`

```rust
pub struct Sticky<W> { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that keeps its contents in view.

When the contents of a [`Sticky`](struct.Sticky.md) widget would go out of view (for example, when they are scrolled out of a [`Scrollable`](struct.Scrollable.md)), they are moved into an [`overlay`](../advanced/overlay/index.md) inside the intersection of the parent’s [`layout.bounds`](../advanced/struct.Layout.md) and the viewport, so that they stay visible at the edge of the viewport.

The contents start floating as soon as any of their edges goes out of the visible bounds, and they are always clamped to the visible bounds, so that they stay inside them.

While they are stuck, the contents keep their original layout: they simply float in a new position.

When the edges of the contents reach the edges of their parent, they stay attached to them: they keep their original bounds, and are clipped to the visible bounds instead.

Once the parent of the contents has gone out of the visible bounds, they stop floating and scroll with it.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{column, container, scrollable, sticky, space};
use iced::Fill;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    scrollable(column![
        sticky(container("I always stay in view!").width(Fill).padding(10)),
        space().height(3000),
    ])
}
```

**Source:** [sticky.rs](../../src/iced_widget/sticky.rs.md) (lines 88)

# `iced::widget::Svg`

```rust
pub struct Svg<'a, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A vector graphics image.

An [`Svg`](struct.Svg.md) image resizes smoothly without losing any quality.

[`Svg`](struct.Svg.md) images can have a considerable rendering cost when resized, specially when they are complex.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::svg;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    svg("tiger.svg")
}
```

**Source:** [svg.rs](../../src/iced_widget/svg.rs.md) (lines 55)

# `iced::widget::TextEditor`

```rust
pub struct TextEditor<'a, Parser, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Parser: Parser,
    Theme: Catalog,
    Renderer: Renderer, { /* private fields */ }
```

A multi-line text input.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text_editor;

struct State {
   content: text_editor::Content,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    Edit(text_editor::Action)
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    text_editor(&state.content)
        .placeholder("Type something here...")
        .on_action(Message::Edit)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::Edit(action) => {
            state.content.perform(action);
        }
    }
}
```

**Source:** [text_editor.rs](../../src/iced_widget/text_editor.rs.md) (lines 91)

# `iced::widget::TextInput`

```rust
pub struct TextInput<'a, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A field that can be filled with text.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text_input;

struct State {
   content: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    ContentChanged(String)
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    text_input("Type something here...", &state.content)
        .on_input(Message::ContentChanged)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::ContentChanged(content) => {
            state.content = content;
        }
    }
}
```

**Source:** [text_input.rs](../../src/iced_widget/text_input.rs.md) (lines 80)

# `iced::widget::Themer`

```rust
pub struct Themer<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Renderer: Renderer, { /* private fields */ }
```

A widget that applies any `Theme` to its contents.

This widget can be useful to leverage multiple `Theme` types in an application.

# `iced::widget::Toggler`

```rust
pub struct Toggler<'a, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A toggler widget.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::toggler;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    TogglerToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    toggler(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::TogglerToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::TogglerToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

**Source:** [toggler.rs](../../src/iced_widget/toggler.rs.md) (lines 78)

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(is_toggled: bool) -> Toggler<'a, Message, Theme>
```

Creates a new [`Toggler`](struct.Toggler.md).

It expects:

- a boolean describing whether the [`Toggler`](struct.Toggler.md) is checked or not
- An optional label for the [`Toggler`](struct.Toggler.md)
- a function that will be called when the [`Toggler`](struct.Toggler.md) is toggled. It will receive the new state of the [`Toggler`](struct.Toggler.md) and must produce a `Message`.

# `iced::widget::Tooltip`

```rust
pub struct Tooltip<'a, W, V, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

An element to display a widget over another.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{container, tooltip};

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    tooltip(
        "Hover me to display the tooltip!",
        container("This is the tooltip contents!")
            .padding(10)
            .style(container::rounded_box),
        tooltip::Position::Bottom,
    )
}
```

# `iced::widget::VerticalSlider`

```rust
pub struct VerticalSlider<'a, T, Message, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

An vertical bar and a handle that selects a single value from a range of values.

A [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md) will try to fill the vertical space of its container.

The [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md) range of numeric values is generic and its step size defaults to 1 unit.

Note: Under the hood values are converted to/from f64 so only values representable exactly as an f64 are possible to select via the slider. However it is likely that the precision of the slider at these scales is already less than the precision lost from the f64 representation.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::vertical_slider;

struct State {
   value: f32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    ValueChanged(f32),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    vertical_slider(0.0..=100.0, state.value, Message::ValueChanged)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::ValueChanged(value) => {
            state.value = value;
        }
    }
}
```

**Source:** [vertical_slider.rs](../../src/iced_widget/vertical_slider.rs.md) (lines 87)

## Methods

### `impl<'a, T, Message, Theme> VerticalSlider<'a, T, Message, Theme> where T: Copy + PartialOrd, Message: Clone, Theme: Catalog,`

#### `DEFAULT_WIDTH`

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_WIDTH: f32 = 16.0
```

The default width of a [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md).

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new<F>( range: RangeInclusive<T>, value: T, on_change: F, ) -> VerticalSlider<'a, T, Message, Theme> where F: 'a + Fn(T) -> Message,
```

Creates a new [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md).

It expects:

- an inclusive range of possible values
- the current value of the [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md)
- a function that will be called when the [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md) is dragged. It receives the new value of the [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md) and must produce a `Message`.

#### `default`

```rust
pub fn default( self, default: impl Into<T>, ) -> VerticalSlider<'a, T, Message, Theme>
```

Sets the optional default value for the [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md).

If set, the [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md) will reset to this value when ctrl-clicked or command-clicked.

#### `on_release`

```rust
pub fn on_release( self, on_release: Message, ) -> VerticalSlider<'a, T, Message, Theme>
```

Sets the release message of the [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md). This is called when the mouse is released from the slider.

Typically, the user’s interaction with the slider is finished when this message is produced. This is useful if you need to spawn a long-running task from the slider’s result, where the default on_change message could create too many events.

# `iced::widget::Component`

```rust
pub trait Component<'a, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Renderer: Renderer, {
    type State: Default + 'static;
    type Event: 'static;

    // Required methods
    fn update(
        &self,
        state: &mut Self::State,
        event: Self::Event,
        renderer: &Renderer,
    ) -> Option<Message>;
    fn view(
        &self,
        state: &Self::State,
    ) -> impl Widget<Self::Event, Theme, Renderer> + 'a;

    // Provided methods
    fn listen(
        &self,
        _state: &Self::State,
        _event: &Event,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Action<Self::Event> { ... }
    fn mouse_interaction(&self, _state: &Self::State) -> Interaction { ... }
    fn diff(&mut self, _state: &mut Self::State) { ... }
    fn operate(
        &self,
        _state: &mut Self::State,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _operation: &mut dyn Operation,
    ) { ... }
}
```

A reusable, custom widget that uses The Elm Architecture.

A [`Component`](trait.Component.md) allows you to implement custom widgets as if they were `iced` applications with encapsulated state.

In other words, a [`Component`](trait.Component.md) allows you to turn `iced` applications into custom widgets and embed them without cumbersome wiring.

A [`Component`](trait.Component.md) produces widgets that may fire an [`Event`](trait.Component.md) and update the internal state of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

Additionally, a [`Component`](trait.Component.md) is capable of producing a `Message` to notify the parent application of any relevant interactions.

## State

A component can store its state in one of two ways: either as data within the implementor of the trait, or in a type [`State`](trait.Component.md) that is managed by the runtime and provided to the trait methods. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and have opposite pros and cons.

For instance, if a piece of state is needed by multiple components that reside in different branches of the tree, then it’s more convenient to let a common ancestor store it and pass it down.

On the other hand, if a piece of state is only needed by the component itself, you can store it as part of its internal [`State`](trait.Component.md).

**Source:** [component.rs](../../src/iced_widget/component.rs.md) (lines 42)

## Required Associated Types

### `State`

```rust
type State: Default + 'static
```

The internal state of this [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

### `Event`

```rust
type Event: 'static
```

The type of event this [`Component`](trait.Component.md) handles internally.

## Required Methods

### `update`

```rust
fn update( &self, state: &mut Self::State, event: Self::Event, renderer: &Renderer, ) -> Option<Message>
```

Processes an [`Event`](trait.Component.md) and updates the [`Component`](trait.Component.md) state accordingly.

It can produce a `Message` for the parent application.

### `view`

```rust
fn view( &self, state: &Self::State, ) -> impl Widget<Self::Event, Theme, Renderer> + 'a
```

Produces the widgets of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md), which may trigger an [`Event`](trait.Component.md) on user interaction.

## Provided Methods

### `listen`

```rust
fn listen( &self, _state: &Self::State, _event: &Event, _bounds: Rectangle, _cursor: Cursor, ) -> Action<Self::Event>
```

Listens to a runtime [`Event`](../enum.Event.md) and performs an [`Action`](struct.Action.md) as a result.

If the [`Action`](struct.Action.md) publishes a [`Component::Event`](trait.Component.md), it will be immediately fed to [`update`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it returns [`Action::none`](struct.Action.md).

### `mouse_interaction`

```rust
fn mouse_interaction(&self, _state: &Self::State) -> Interaction
```

Returns the current [`mouse::Interaction`](../mouse/enum.Interaction.md) of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

This interaction will override any interaction produced by the [`view`](trait.Component.md) of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it returns [`mouse::Interaction::None`](../mouse/enum.Interaction.md).

### `diff`

```rust
fn diff(&mut self, _state: &mut Self::State)
```

Reconciles the current [`Component`](trait.Component.md) with its internal [`State`](trait.Component.md) persisted in the widget tree.

This method will be called every time the widget tree changes. You can leverage it to detect and react to changes in the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it does nothing.

### `operate`

```rust
fn operate( &self, _state: &mut Self::State, _bounds: Rectangle, _operation: &mut dyn Operation, )
```

Run the provided [`widget::Operation`](../advanced/widget/trait.Operation.md) on the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it does nothing.

# `iced::window::frames`

```rust
pub fn frames() -> Subscription<Instant>
```

Subscribes to the frames of the window of the running application.

The resulting [`Subscription`](../struct.Subscription.md) will produce items at a rate equal to the refresh rate of the first application window. Note that this rate may be variable, as it is normally managed by the graphics driver and/or the OS.

In any case, this [`Subscription`](../struct.Subscription.md) is useful to smoothly draw application-driven animations without missing any frames.

# `iced::window::request_user_attention`

```rust
pub fn request_user_attention<T>(
    id: Id,
    user_attention: Option<UserAttention>,
) -> Task<T>
```

Requests user attention to the window. This has no effect if the application is already focused. How requesting for user attention manifests is platform dependent, see [`UserAttention`](enum.UserAttention.md) for details.

Providing `None` will unset the request for user attention. Unsetting the request for user attention might not be done automatically by the WM when the window receives input.

# `iced::window`

Configure the window of your application in native platforms.

## Modules

- [`icon`](icon/index.md) — Attach an icon to the window of your application.
- [`raw_window_handle`](raw_window_handle/index.md) — Interoperability library for Rust Windowing applications.
- [`screenshot`](screenshot/index.md) — Take screenshots of a window.
- [`settings`](settings/index.md) — Configure your windows.

## Structs

- [`Headless`](struct.Headless.md) — A headless window.
- [`Icon`](struct.Icon.md) — An window icon normally used for the titlebar or taskbar.
- [`Id`](struct.Id.md) — The id of the window.
- [`Screenshot`](struct.Screenshot.md) — Data of a screenshot, captured with `window::screenshot()`.
- [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md) — The window settings of an application.

## Enums

- [`Action`](enum.Action.md) — An operation to be performed on some window.
- [`Direction`](enum.Direction.md) — The cardinal directions relative to the center of a window.
- [`Event`](enum.Event.md) — A window-related event.
- [`Level`](enum.Level.md) — A window level groups windows with respect to their z-position.
- [`Mode`](enum.Mode.md) — The mode of a window-based application.
- [`Position`](enum.Position.md) — The position of a window in a given screen.
- [`RedrawRequest`](enum.RedrawRequest.md) — A request to redraw a window.
- [`UserAttention`](enum.UserAttention.md) — The type of user attention to request.

## Traits

- [`Window`](trait.Window.md) — A window managed by iced.

## Functions

- [`frames`](fn.frames.md) — Subscribes to the frames of the window of the running application.

- [`is_minimized`](fn.is_minimized.md) — Gets the minimized state of the window with the given [`Id`](struct.Id.md).

# `iced::advanced::subscription::Recipe`

```rust
pub trait Recipe {
    type Output;

    // Required methods
    fn hash(&self, state: &mut FxHasher);
    fn stream(
        self: Box<Self>,
        input: Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = Event> + Send>>,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = Self::Output> + Send>>;
}
```

The description of a [`Subscription`](../../struct.Subscription.md).

A [`Recipe`](trait.Recipe.md) is the internal definition of a [`Subscription`](../../struct.Subscription.md). It is used by runtimes to run and identify subscriptions. You can use it to create your own!

## Required Associated Types

### `Output`

```rust
type Output
```

The events that will be produced by a [`Subscription`](../../struct.Subscription.md) with this [`Recipe`](trait.Recipe.md).

## Required Methods

### `hash`

```rust
fn hash(&self, state: &mut FxHasher)
```

Hashes the [`Recipe`](trait.Recipe.md).

This is used by runtimes to uniquely identify a [`Subscription`](../../struct.Subscription.md).

### `stream`

```rust
fn stream( self: Box<Self>, input: Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = Event> + Send>>, ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = Self::Output> + Send>>
```

# `iced::advanced::widget`

Create custom widgets and operate on them.

## Modules

- [`operation`](operation/index.md) — Query or update internal widget state.
- [`text`](text/index.md) — Text widgets display information through writing.
- [`tree`](tree/index.md) — Store internal widget state in a state tree to ensure continuity.

## Structs

- [`Element`](struct.Element.md) — A generic [`Widget`](../trait.Widget.md).
- [`Id`](struct.Id.md) — The identifier of a generic widget.
- [`Map`](struct.Map.md) — A [`Widget`](../trait.Widget.md) that transforms the produced message of another widget.
- [`Text`](struct.Text.md) — A bunch of text.
- [`Tree`](struct.Tree.md) — A persistent state widget tree.
- [`Void`](struct.Void.md) — A zero-sized [`Widget`](../trait.Widget.md) that does nothing and will be filtered out by containers.

## Traits

- [`Meta`](trait.Meta.md) — Metadata of a [`Widget`](../trait.Widget.md), independent of its generic parameters.
- [`Operation`](trait.Operation.md) — A piece of logic that can traverse the widget tree of an application in order to query or update some widget state.
- [`Widget`](trait.Widget.md) — A component that displays information and allows interaction.

## Functions

- [`operate`](fn.operate.md) — Creates a new [`Task`](../../struct.Task.md) that runs the given [`widget::Operation`](trait.Operation.md) and produces its output.

# `iced::advanced::widget::Operation`

```rust
pub trait Operation<T = ()>: Send {
    // Required method
    fn traverse(&mut self, operate: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut dyn Operation<T>));

    // Provided methods
    fn container(
        &mut self,
        _id: Option<&Id>,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _viewport: &Rectangle,
    ) { ... }
    fn scrollable(
        &mut self,
        _id: Option<&Id>,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _content: Size,
        _translation: Vector,
        _state: &mut dyn Scrollable,
    ) { ... }
    fn focusable(
        &mut self,
        _id: Option<&Id>,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _state: &mut dyn Focusable,
    ) { ... }
    fn text_input(
        &mut self,
        _id: Option<&Id>,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _state: &mut dyn TextInput,
    ) { ... }
    fn text(
        &mut self,
        _id: Option<&Id>,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _state: &mut dyn Text,
    ) { ... }
    fn custom(
        &mut self,
        _id: Option<&Id>,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _state: &mut (dyn Any + 'static),
    ) { ... }
    fn finish(&self) -> Outcome<T> { ... }
}
```

A piece of logic that can traverse the widget tree of an application in order to query or update some widget state.

## Required Methods

### `traverse`

```rust
fn traverse(&mut self, operate: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut dyn Operation<T>))
```

Requests further traversal of the widget tree to keep operating.

The provided `operate` closure may be called by an [`Operation`](trait.Operation.md) to return control to the widget tree and keep traversing it. If the closure is not called, the children of the widget asking for traversal will be skipped.

## Provided Methods

### `container`

```rust
fn container( &mut self, _id: Option<&Id>, _bounds: Rectangle, _viewport: &Rectangle, )
```

Operates on a widget that contains other widgets.

### `scrollable`

```rust
fn scrollable( &mut self, _id: Option<&Id>, _bounds: Rectangle, _content: Size, _translation: Vector, _state: &mut dyn Scrollable, )
```

Operates on a widget that can be scrolled.

### `focusable`

```rust
fn focusable( &mut self, _id: Option<&Id>, _bounds: Rectangle, _state: &mut dyn Focusable, )
```

Operates on a widget that can be focused.

### `text_input`

```rust
fn text_input( &mut self, _id: Option<&Id>, _bounds: Rectangle, _state: &mut dyn TextInput, )
```

Operates on a widget that has text input.

### `text`

```rust
fn text(&mut self, _id: Option<&Id>, _bounds: Rectangle, _state: &mut dyn Text)
```

Operates on a widget that contains some text.

### `custom`

```rust
fn custom( &mut self, _id: Option<&Id>, _bounds: Rectangle, _state: &mut (dyn Any + 'static), )
```

Operates on a custom widget with some state.

### `finish`

```rust
fn finish(&self) -> Outcome<T>
```

Finishes the [`Operation`](trait.Operation.md) and returns its [`Outcome`](operation/enum.Outcome.md).

# `iced::application::timed::timed`

```rust
pub fn timed<State, Message, Theme, Renderer>(
    boot: impl BootFn<State, Message>,
    update: impl UpdateFn<State, Message>,
    subscription: impl Fn(&State) -> Subscription<Message>,
    view: impl for<'a> ViewFn<'a, State, Message, Theme, Renderer>,
) -> Application<impl Program<State = State, Message = (Message, Instant), Theme = Theme>> where
    State: 'static,
    Message: Send + 'static,
    Theme: Base + 'static,
    Renderer: Renderer + 'static,
```

Creates an [`Application`](../struct.Application.md) with an `update` function that also takes the [`Instant`](../../time/struct.Instant.md) of each `Message`.

This constructor is useful to create animated applications that are *pure* (e.g. without relying on side-effect calls like [`Instant::now`](../../time/struct.Instant.md)).

Purity is needed when you want your application to end up in the same exact state given the same history of messages. This property enables proper time traveling debugging with [`comet`](https://github.com/iced-rs/comet).

**Source:** [timed.rs](../../../src/iced/application/timed.rs.md) (lines 21-127)

# `iced::theme::palette`

Define the colors of a theme.

## Structs

- [`Background`](struct.Background.md) — A set of background colors.
- [`Pair`](struct.Pair.md) — A pair of background and text colors.
- [`Palette`](struct.Palette.md) — An extended set of colors generated from a [`Seed`](struct.Seed.md).
- [`Seed`](struct.Seed.md) — The base set of colors of a [`Palette`](../struct.Palette.md).
- [`Swatch`](struct.Swatch.md) — A color sample in a palette of colors.

# `iced::widget::button`

Buttons allow your users to perform actions by pressing them.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::button;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    ButtonPressed,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    button("Press me!").on_press(Message::ButtonPressed)
}
```

## Structs

- [`Button`](struct.Button.md) — A generic widget that produces a message when pressed.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The style of a button.

## Enums

## Constants

## Traits

## Functions

- [`danger`](fn.danger.md) — A danger button; denoting a destructive action.
- [`primary`](fn.primary.md) — A primary button; denoting a main action.
- [`secondary`](fn.secondary.md) — A secondary button; denoting a complementary action.
- [`subtle`](fn.subtle.md) — A subtle button using weak background shades.
- [`success`](fn.success.md) — A success button; denoting a good outcome.
- [`text`](fn.text.md) — A text button; useful for links.

# `iced::widget::canvas`

Canvases can be leveraged to draw interactive 2D graphics.

## Example: Drawing a Simple Circle

```rust
use iced::mouse;
use iced::widget::canvas;
use iced::{Color, Rectangle, Renderer, Theme};

// First, we define the data we need for drawing
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Circle {
    radius: f32,
}

// Then, we implement the `Program` trait
impl<Message> canvas::Program<Message> for Circle {
    // No internal state
    type State = ();

    fn draw(
        &self,
        _state: &(),
        renderer: &Renderer,
        _theme: &Theme,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: mouse::Cursor
    ) -> Vec<canvas::Geometry> {
        // We prepare a new `Frame`
        let mut frame = canvas::Frame::new(renderer, bounds.size());

        // We create a `Path` representing a simple circle
        let circle = canvas::Path::circle(frame.center(), self.radius);

        // And fill it with some color
        frame.fill(&circle, Color::BLACK);

        // Then, we produce the geometry
        vec![frame.into_geometry()]
    }
}

// Finally, we simply use our `Circle` to create the `Canvas`!
fn view<Message>(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    canvas(Circle { radius: 50.0 })
}
```

## Modules

- [`fill`](fill/index.md) — Fill `Geometry` with a certain style.
- [`gradient`](gradient/index.md) — A gradient that can be used as a fill for some geometry.
- [`path`](path/index.md) — Build different kinds of 2D shapes.
- [`stroke`](stroke/index.md) — Create lines from a [`Path`](struct.Path.md) and assigns them various attributes/styles.

- [`Action`](struct.Action.md) — A runtime action that can be performed by some widgets.

- [`Group`](struct.Group.md) — A cache group.
- [`Image`](struct.Image.md) — A raster image that can be drawn.
- [`LineDash`](struct.LineDash.md) — The dash pattern used when stroking the line.
- [`Path`](struct.Path.md) — An immutable set of points that may or may not be connected.
- [`Stroke`](struct.Stroke.md) — The style of a stroke.
- [`Text`](struct.Text.md) — A bunch of text that can be drawn to a canvas
