# `iced::widget::canvas::Program`

```rust
pub trait Program<Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> where
    Renderer: Renderer, {
    type State: Default + 'static;

    // Required method
    fn draw(
        &self,
        state: &Self::State,
        renderer: &Renderer,
        theme: &Theme,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Vec<<Renderer as Renderer>::Geometry>;

    // Provided methods
    fn update(
        &self,
        _state: &mut Self::State,
        _event: &Event,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Option<Action<Message>> { ... }
    fn mouse_interaction(
        &self,
        _state: &Self::State,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Interaction { ... }
}
```

The state and logic of a [`Canvas`](../struct.Canvas.md).

A [`Program`](trait.Program.md) can mutate internal state and produce messages for an application.

**Source:** [program.rs](../../../src/iced_widget/canvas/program.rs.md) (lines 13)

## Required Associated Types

### `State`

```rust
type State: Default + 'static
```

The internal state mutated by the [`Program`](trait.Program.md).

## Required Methods

### `draw`

```rust
fn draw( &self, state: &Self::State, renderer: &Renderer, theme: &Theme, bounds: Rectangle, cursor: Cursor, ) -> Vec<<Renderer as Renderer>::Geometry>
```

Draws the state of the [`Program`](trait.Program.md), producing a bunch of [`Geometry`](type.Geometry.md).

[`Geometry`](type.Geometry.md) can be easily generated with a [`Frame`](type.Frame.md) or stored in a [`Cache`](type.Cache.md).

## Provided Methods

### `update`

```rust
fn update( &self, _state: &mut Self::State, _event: &Event, _bounds: Rectangle, _cursor: Cursor, ) -> Option<Action<Message>>
```

Updates the [`State`](trait.Program.md) of the [`Program`](trait.Program.md).

When a [`Program`](trait.Program.md) is used in a [`Canvas`](../struct.Canvas.md), the runtime will call this method for each [`Event`](../../enum.Event.md).

This method can optionally return an [`Action`](../struct.Action.md) to either notify an application of any meaningful interactions, capture the event, or request a redraw.

By default, this method does and returns nothing.

### `mouse_interaction`

```rust
fn mouse_interaction( &self, _state: &Self::State, _bounds: Rectangle, _cursor: Cursor, ) -> Interaction
```

Returns the current mouse interaction of the [`Program`](trait.Program.md).

The interaction returned will be in effect even if the cursor position is out of bounds of the program’s [`Canvas`](../struct.Canvas.md).

# `iced::widget::canvas::Cache`

```rust
pub type Cache<Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>> = Cache<Renderer>;
```

A simple cache that stores generated [`Geometry`](type.Geometry.md) to avoid recomputation.

A [`Cache`](type.Cache.md) will not redraw its geometry unless the dimensions of its layer change or it is explicitly cleared.

# `iced::widget::checkbox`

Checkboxes can be used to let users make binary choices.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::checkbox;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    CheckboxToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    checkbox(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::CheckboxToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::CheckboxToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

![Checkbox drawn by iced_wgpu](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced/blob/7760618fb112074bc40b148944521f312152012a/docs/images/checkbox.png?raw=true)

## Structs

- [`Icon`](struct.Icon.md) — The icon in a [`Checkbox`](../struct.Checkbox.md).
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The style of a checkbox.

## Enums

- [`Status`](enum.Status.md) — The possible status of a [`Checkbox`](../struct.Checkbox.md).

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`Checkbox`](../struct.Checkbox.md).

## Functions

- [`danger`](fn.danger.md) — A danger checkbox; denoting a negative toggle.
- [`primary`](fn.primary.md) — A primary checkbox; denoting a main toggle.
- [`secondary`](fn.secondary.md) — A secondary checkbox; denoting a complementary toggle.
- [`success`](fn.success.md) — A success checkbox; denoting a positive toggle.

## Type Aliases

# `iced::widget::combo_box`

Combo boxes display a dropdown list of searchable and selectable options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::combo_box;

struct State {
   fruits: combo_box::State<Fruit>,
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    combo_box(
        &state.fruits,
        "Select your favorite fruit...",
        state.favorite.as_ref(),
        Message::FruitSelected
    )
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`ComboBox`](struct.ComboBox.md) — A widget for searching and selecting a single value from a list of options.
- [`State`](struct.State.md) — The local state of a [`ComboBox`](../struct.ComboBox.md).

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`ComboBox`](../struct.ComboBox.md).

# `iced::widget::container`

Containers let you align a widget inside their boundaries.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::container;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    container("This text is centered inside a rounded box!")
        .padding(10)
        .center(800)
        .style(container::rounded_box)
}
```

## Structs

- [`Container`](struct.Container.md) — A widget that aligns its contents inside of its boundaries.

# `iced::widget::image`

Images display raster graphics in different formats (PNG, JPG, etc.).

## Modules

- [`viewer`](viewer/index.md) — Zoom and pan on an image.

## Structs

- [`Allocation`](struct.Allocation.md) — A memory allocation of a [`Handle`](../../advanced/image/enum.Handle.md), often in GPU memory.
- [`Image`](struct.Image.md) — A frame that displays an image while keeping aspect ratio.
- [`Viewer`](struct.Viewer.md) — A frame that displays an image with the ability to zoom in/out and pan.

## Enums

- [`Error`](enum.Error.md) — An image loading error.
- [`FilterMethod`](enum.FilterMethod.md) — Image filtering strategy.
- [`Handle`](enum.Handle.md) — A handle of some image data.

## Functions

- [`draw`](fn.draw.md) — Draws an [`Image`](../struct.Image.md)
- [`layout`](fn.layout.md) — Computes the layout of an [`Image`](../struct.Image.md).
- [`viewer`](fn.viewer.md) — Creates a new [`Viewer`](struct.Viewer.md) with the given image `Handle`.

# `iced::widget::keyed`

Keyed widgets can provide hints to ensure continuity.

## What is continuity?

Continuity is the feeling of persistence of state.

In a graphical user interface, users expect widgets to have a certain degree of continuous state. For instance, a text input that is focused should stay focused even if the widget tree changes slightly.

Continuity is tricky in `iced` and the Elm Architecture because the whole widget tree is rebuilt during every `view` call. This is very convenient from a developer perspective because you can build extremely dynamic interfaces without worrying about changing state.

However, the tradeoff is that determining what changed becomes hard for `iced`. If you have a list of things, adding an element at the top may cause a loss of continuity on every element on the list!

## How can we keep continuity?

The good news is that user interfaces generally have a static widget structure. This structure can be relied on to ensure some degree of continuity. `iced` already does this.

However, sometimes you have a certain part of your interface that is quite dynamic. For instance, a list of things where items may be added or removed at any place.

There are different ways to mitigate this during the reconciliation stage, but they involve comparing trees at certain depths and backtracking… Quite computationally expensive.

One approach that is cheaper consists in letting the user provide some hints about the identities of the different widgets so that they can be compared directly without going deeper.

The widgets in this module will all ask for a “hint” of some sort. In order to help them keep continuity, you need to make sure the hint stays the same for the same items in your user interface between `view` calls.

## Modules

- [`column`](column/index.md) — Keyed columns distribute content vertically while keeping continuity.

## Structs

- [`Column`](struct.Column.md) — A container that distributes its contents vertically while keeping continuity.

# `iced::widget::keyed::Column`

```rust
pub struct Column<Key, W> where
    Key: Copy + PartialEq, { /* private fields */ }
```

A container that distributes its contents vertically while keeping continuity.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{keyed_column, text};

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    keyed_column((0..=100).map(|i| {
        (i, text!("Item {i}"))
    }))
}
```

**Source:** [column.rs](../../../src/iced_widget/keyed/column.rs.md) (lines 31)

#### `from_vecs`

Creates a [`Column`](struct.Column.md) from already allocated [`Vec`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)s.

Keep in mind that the [`Column`](struct.Column.md) will not inspect the [`Vec`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)s, which means it won’t automatically adapt to the sizing strategy of its contents.

If any of the children have a [`Length::Fill`](../../enum.Length.md) strategy, you will need to call [`Column::width`](struct.Column.md) or [`Column::height`](struct.Column.md) accordingly.

# `iced::widget::markdown::Item`

```rust
pub enum Item {
    Heading(HeadingLevel, Text),
    Paragraph(Text),
    CodeBlock {
        language: Option<String>,
        code: String,
        lines: Vec<Text>,
    },
    List {
        start: Option<u64>,
        bullets: Vec<Bullet>,
    },
    Image {
        url: String,
        title: String,
        alt: Text,
    },
    Quote(Vec<Item>),
    Rule,
    Table {
        columns: Vec<Column>,
        rows: Vec<Row>,
    },
}
```

A Markdown item.

**Source:** [markdown.rs](../../../src/iced_widget/markdown.rs.md) (lines 730)

## Variants

### `Heading(HeadingLevel, Text)`

A heading.

### `Paragraph(Text)`

A paragraph.

### `CodeBlock`

A code block.

You can enable the `highlighter` feature for syntax highlighting.

**Fields**

- `language: Option<String>` — The language of the code block, if any.
- `code: String` — The raw code of the code block.
- `lines: Vec<Text>` — The styled lines of text in the code block.

### `List`

A list.

**Fields**

- `start: Option<u64>` — The first number of the list, if it is ordered.
- `bullets: Vec<Bullet>` — The items of the list.

### `Image`

An image.

**Fields**

- `url: String` — The destination URL of the image.
- `title: String` — The title of the image.
- `alt: Text` — The alternative text of the image.

### `Quote(Vec<Item>)`

A quote.

### `Rule`

A horizontal separator.

### `Table`

A table.

**Fields**

- `columns: Vec<Column>` — The columns of the table.
- `rows: Vec<Row>` — The rows of the table.

# `iced::widget::markdown::parse`

```rust
pub fn parse(markdown: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = Item>
```

Parse the given Markdown content.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::markdown;
use iced::{Theme, Widget};

struct State {
   markdown: Vec<markdown::Item>,
}

enum Message {
    LinkClicked(markdown::Uri),
}

impl State {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            markdown: markdown::parse("This is some **Markdown**!").collect(),
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message> {
        markdown::view(
            &self.markdown,
            markdown::Settings::default(),
            Theme::TokyoNight,
        )
            .map(Message::LinkClicked)
    }

    fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::LinkClicked(url) => {
                println!("The following url was clicked: {url}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Source:** [markdown.rs](../../../src/iced_widget/markdown.rs.md) (lines 1001)

# `iced::widget::markdown`

Markdown widgets can parse and display Markdown.

You can enable the `highlighter` feature for syntax highlighting in code blocks.

Only the variants of [`Item`](enum.Item.md) are currently supported.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::markdown;
use iced::{Theme, Widget};

struct State {
   markdown: Vec<markdown::Item>,
}

enum Message {
    LinkClicked(markdown::Uri),
}

impl State {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            markdown: markdown::parse("This is some **Markdown**!").collect(),
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message> {
        markdown::view(
            &self.markdown,
            markdown::Settings::default(),
            Theme::TokyoNight,
        )
            .map(Message::LinkClicked)
    }

    fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::LinkClicked(url) => {
                println!("The following url was clicked: {url}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`Column`](struct.Column.md) — The column of a table.
- [`Content`](struct.Content.md) — A bunch of Markdown that has been parsed.
- [`DefaultViewer`](struct.DefaultViewer.md) — The default [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md).
- [`Highlight`](struct.Highlight.md) — A text highlight.
- [`InlineCode`](struct.InlineCode.md) — The style of some inline code.
- [`Row`](struct.Row.md) — The row of a table.
- [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md) — Configuration controlling Markdown rendering in [`view`](../fn.markdown.md).
- [`Text`](struct.Text.md) — A bunch of parsed Markdown text.

## Enums

- [`Bullet`](enum.Bullet.md) — The item of a list.
- [`HeadingLevel`](enum.HeadingLevel.md)
- [`Item`](enum.Item.md) — A Markdown item.

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of Markdown items.
- [`Highlighter`](trait.Highlighter.md) — A type that describes how to highlight an `Input` with some [`Style`](../../advanced/text/highlighter/struct.Style.md).
- [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) — A view strategy to display a Markdown [`Item`](enum.Item.md).

## Functions

- [`code_block`](fn.code_block.md) — Displays a code block using the default look.
- [`heading`](fn.heading.md) — Displays a heading using the default look.
- [`item`](fn.item.md) — Displays an [`Item`](enum.Item.md) using the given [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md).
- [`items`](fn.items.md) — Displays a column of items with the default look.
- [`ordered_list`](fn.ordered_list.md) — Displays an ordered list using the default look and calling the [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) for each numbered item.
- [`paragraph`](fn.paragraph.md) — Displays a paragraph using the default look.
- [`parse`](fn.parse.md) — Parse the given Markdown content.
- [`quote`](fn.quote.md) — Displays a quote using the default look.
- [`rule`](fn.rule.md) — Displays a rule using the default look.
- [`sections`](fn.sections.md) — Groups the given Markdown [`Item`](enum.Item.md)s by [`Item::Heading`](enum.Item.md).
- [`table`](fn.table.md) — Displays a table using the default look.
- [`unordered_list`](fn.unordered_list.md) — Displays an unordered list using the default look and calling the [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) for each bullet point item.
- [`view`](fn.view.md) — Display a bunch of Markdown items.
- [`view_with`](fn.view_with.md) — Runs [`view`](../fn.markdown.md) but with a custom [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) to turn an [`Item`](enum.Item.md) into a widget.

## Type Aliases

# `iced::widget::markdown::Viewer`

```rust
pub trait Viewer<'a, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer<Renderer, Renderer>>: Sized + 'awhere
    Message: 'a,
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
    Renderer: Renderer + 'a, {

    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn unordered_list(

    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }

        &self,

        rows: &'a [Row],
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }

```

A view strategy to display a Markdown [`Item`](enum.Item.md).

A [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) is in charge of turning each [`Item`](enum.Item.md) into a widget. It also provides the [`Theme`](../../enum.Theme.md) and [`text::Highlighter`](../../advanced/text/trait.Highlighter.md) used for rendering.

# `iced::widget::pane_grid`

Pane grids let your users split regions of your application and organize layout dynamically.

![Pane grid - Iced](https://iced.rs/examples/pane_grid.gif)

This distribution of space is common in tiling window managers (like [`awesome`](https://awesomewm.org/), [`i3`](https://i3wm.org/), or even [`tmux`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux)).

A [`PaneGrid`](../struct.PaneGrid.md) supports:

- Vertical and horizontal splits
- Tracking of the last active pane
- Mouse-based resizing
- Drag and drop to reorganize panes
- Hotkey support
- Configurable modifier keys
- [`State`](struct.State.md) API to perform actions programmatically (`split`, `swap`, `resize`, etc.)

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{pane_grid, text};

struct State {
    panes: pane_grid::State<Pane>,
}

enum Pane {
    SomePane,
    AnotherKindOfPane,
}

enum Message {
    PaneDragged(pane_grid::DragEvent),
    PaneResized(pane_grid::ResizeEvent),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    pane_grid(&state.panes, |pane, state, is_maximized| {
        pane_grid::Content::new(match state {
            Pane::SomePane => text("This is some pane"),
            Pane::AnotherKindOfPane => text("This is another kind of pane"),
        })
    })
    .on_drag(Message::PaneDragged)
    .on_resize(10, Message::PaneResized)
}
```

The [`pane_grid` example](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced/tree/master/examples/pane_grid) showcases how to use a [`PaneGrid`](../struct.PaneGrid.md) with resizing, drag and drop, and hotkey support.

## Modules

- [`state`](state/index.md) — The state of a [`PaneGrid`](../struct.PaneGrid.md).

# `iced::widget::pane_grid::State`

```rust
pub struct State<T> {
    pub panes: BTreeMap<Pane, T>,
    pub internal: Internal,
}
```

The state of a [`PaneGrid`](../struct.PaneGrid.md).

It keeps track of the state of each [`Pane`](struct.Pane.md) and the position of each [`Split`](struct.Split.md).

The [`State`](struct.State.md) needs to own any mutable contents a [`Pane`](struct.Pane.md) may need. This is why this struct is generic over the type `T`. Values of this type are provided to the view function of [`PaneGrid::new`](../struct.PaneGrid.md) for displaying each [`Pane`](struct.Pane.md).

**Source:** [state.rs](../../../src/iced_widget/pane_grid/state.rs.md) (lines 23)

## Fields

### `panes: BTreeMap<Pane, T>`

The panes of the [`PaneGrid`](../struct.PaneGrid.md).

### `internal: Internal`

The internal state of the [`PaneGrid`](../struct.PaneGrid.md).

Convert `Box<dyn Trait>` (where `Trait: Downcast`) to `Box<dyn Any>`. `Box<dyn Any>` can then be further `downcast` into `Box<ConcreteType>` where `ConcreteType` implements `Trait`.

#### `into_any_rc`

```rust
fn into_any_rc(self: Rc<T>) -> Rc<dyn Any>
```

Convert `Rc<Trait>` (where `Trait: Downcast`) to `Rc<Any>`. `Rc<Any>` can then be further `downcast` into `Rc<ConcreteType>` where `ConcreteType` implements `Trait`.

#### `as_any`

```rust
fn as_any(&self) -> &(dyn Any + 'static)
```

Convert `&Trait` (where `Trait: Downcast`) to `&Any`. This is needed since Rust cannot generate `&Any`’s vtable from `&Trait`’s.

#### `as_any_mut`

```rust
fn as_any_mut(&mut self) -> &mut (dyn Any + 'static)
```

Convert `&mut Trait` (where `Trait: Downcast`) to `&Any`. This is needed since Rust cannot generate `&mut Any`’s vtable from `&mut Trait`’s.

# `iced::widget::pick_list`

Pick lists display a dropdown list of selectable options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::pick_list;

struct State {
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let fruits = [
        Fruit::Apple,
        Fruit::Orange,
        Fruit::Strawberry,
        Fruit::Tomato,
    ];

    pick_list(
        state.favorite,
        fruits,
        Fruit::to_string,
    )
    .on_select(Message::FruitSelected)
    .placeholder("Select your favorite fruit...")
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`Icon`](struct.Icon.md) — The icon of a [`Handle`](enum.Handle.md).
- [`PickList`](struct.PickList.md) — A widget for selecting a single value from a list of options.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of a pick list.

## Enums

## Traits

# `iced::widget::radio`

Radio buttons let users choose a single option from a bunch of options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{column, radio};

struct State {
   selection: Option<Choice>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum Message {
    RadioSelected(Choice),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Choice {
    A,
    B,
    C,
    All,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let a = radio(
        "A",
        Choice::A,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let b = radio(
        "B",
        Choice::B,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let c = radio(
        "C",
        Choice::C,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let all = radio(
        "All of the above",
        Choice::All,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected
    );

    column![a, b, c, all]
}
```

## Structs

- [`Radio`](struct.Radio.md) — A circular button representing a choice.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of a radio button.

## Enums

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`Radio`](../struct.Radio.md).

## Functions

- [`default`](fn.default.md) — The default style of a [`Radio`](../struct.Radio.md) button.

## Type Aliases

- [`StyleFn`](type.StyleFn.md) — A styling function for a [`Radio`](../struct.Radio.md).

```rust
pub enum Candidate<'a> {
    Container {
        id: Option<&'a Id>,

        visible_bounds: Option<Rectangle>,

    },
    Custom {
        id: Option<&'a Id>,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        visible_bounds: Option<Rectangle>,
        state: &'a (dyn Any + 'static),
```

# `iced::widget::slider`

Sliders let users set a value by moving an indicator.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::slider;

struct State {
   value: f32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    ValueChanged(f32),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    slider(0.0..=100.0, state.value, Message::ValueChanged)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::ValueChanged(value) => {
            state.value = value;
        }
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`Handle`](struct.Handle.md) — The appearance of the handle of a slider.
- [`Rail`](struct.Rail.md) — The appearance of a slider rail
- [`Slider`](struct.Slider.md) — An horizontal bar and a handle that selects a single value from a range of values.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of a slider.

# `iced::widget::sticky`

Stick elements to the viewport!

[`Sticky`](../struct.Sticky.md) keeps its contents visible when they would otherwise go out of view, for example when they are scrolled out of a [`Scrollable`](../struct.Scrollable.md). As soon as any of the contents’ edges goes out of the visible bounds, they are moved into an [`overlay`](../../advanced/overlay/index.md) inside the visible bounds, so that they stay at the edge of the viewport.

While they are stuck, the contents keep their original layout: they simply float in a new position, inside the visible bounds.

When the edges of the contents reach the edges of their parent, they stay attached to them: they keep their original bounds, and are clipped to the visible bounds instead.

Once the parent of the contents has gone out of the visible bounds, they stop floating and scroll with it.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{column, container, scrollable, sticky, space};
use iced::Fill;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    scrollable(column![
        sticky(container("I always stay in view!").width(Fill).padding(10)),
        space().height(3000),
    ])
}
```

## Structs

- [`Sticky`](struct.Sticky.md) — A widget that keeps its contents in view.

---

# `iced::widget::text`

Draw and interact with text.

## Modules

- [`highlighter`](highlighter/index.md) — Highlight text.

## Structs

- [`Format`](struct.Format.md) — The format of some [`Text`](../../advanced/widget/struct.Text.md).
- [`Operand`](struct.Operand.md) — The state of a widget with text, operated on by [`super::Operation::text`](../../advanced/widget/trait.Operation.md).
- [`Position`](struct.Position.md) — A specific position in some [`Text`](../../advanced/struct.Text.md).
- [`Rich`](struct.Rich.md) — A bunch of [`Rich`](struct.Rich.md) text.
- [`Span`](struct.Span.md) — A span of text.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of some text.

## Enums

- [`Alignment`](enum.Alignment.md) — The alignment of some text.
- [`Ellipsis`](enum.Ellipsis.md) — The ellipsis strategy of some text.
- [`LineHeight`](enum.LineHeight.md) — The height of a line of text in a paragraph.
- [`Shaping`](enum.Shaping.md) — The shaping strategy of some text.
- [`Wrapping`](enum.Wrapping.md) — The wrapping strategy of some text.

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`Text`](../../advanced/widget/struct.Text.md).
- [`Highlighter`](trait.Highlighter.md) — A type that describes how to highlight an `Input` with some [`Style`](../../advanced/text/highlighter/struct.Style.md).
- [`IntoFragment`](trait.IntoFragment.md) — A trait for converting a value to some text [`Fragment`](../../advanced/text/type.Fragment.md).
- [`Parser`](trait.Parser.md) — A type capable of parsing text, producing some `Output`.

## Functions

- [`base`](fn.base.md) — Text with the default base color.
- [`danger`](fn.danger.md) — Text conveying some negative information, like an error.
- [`default`](fn.default.md) — The default text styling; color is inherited.
- [`draw`](fn.draw.md) — Draws text using the same logic as the [`Text`](../../advanced/widget/struct.Text.md) widget.
- [`layout`](fn.layout.md) — Computes the [`Size`](../../struct.Size.md) of a [`Text`](../../advanced/widget/struct.Text.md) widget.
- [`primary`](fn.primary.md) — Text conveying some important information, like an action.
- [`secondary`](fn.secondary.md) — Text conveying some secondary information, like a footnote.
- [`success`](fn.success.md) — Text conveying some positive information, like a successful event.
- [`warning`](fn.warning.md) — Text conveying some mildly negative information, like a warning.

## Type Aliases

- [`Fragment`](type.Fragment.md) — A fragment of [`Text`](../../advanced/struct.Text.md).
- [`StyleFn`](type.StyleFn.md) — A styling function for a [`Text`](../../advanced/widget/struct.Text.md).
- [`Text`](type.Text.md) — A bunch of text.

# `iced::widget::text_editor::Binding`

```rust
pub enum Binding<Message> {
Show 21 variants    Unfocus,
    Copy,
    Cut,
    Paste,
    Undo,
    Redo,
    Move(Motion),
    Select(Motion),
    SelectWord,
    SelectLine,
    SelectAll,
    Insert(char),
    Enter,
    Backspace,
    BackspaceWord,
    BackspaceLine,
    Delete,
    DeleteWord,
    DeleteLine,
    Sequence(Vec<Binding<Message>>),
    Custom(Message),
}
```

A binding to an action in the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

## Variants

### `Unfocus`

Unfocus the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

### `Copy`

Copy the selection of the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

### `Cut`

Cut the selection of the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

### `Paste`

Paste the clipboard contents in the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

### `Undo`

Undo the last change peformed in the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

### `Redo`

Redo the last change undone in the [`Editor`](../../advanced/text/trait.Editor.md).

### `Move(Motion)`

Apply a [`Motion`](enum.Motion.md).

### `Select(Motion)`

Select text with a given [`Motion`](enum.Motion.md).

### `SelectWord`

Select the word at the current cursor.

### `SelectLine`

Select the line at the current cursor.

### `SelectAll`

Select the entire buffer.

### `Insert(char)`

Insert the given character.

### `Enter`

Break the current line.

### `Backspace`

Delete the previous character.

### `BackspaceWord`

Delete the word before the cursor.

### `BackspaceLine`

Delete the line before the cursor.

### `Delete`

Delete the next character.

### `DeleteWord`

Delete the word after the cursor.

### `DeleteLine`

Delete the line after the cursor.

### `Sequence(Vec<Binding<Message>>)`

A sequence of bindings to execute.

### `Custom(Message)`

Produce the given message.

## Methods

### `impl<Message> Binding<Message>`


*Available on crate feature advanced only.*

Returns the default [`Binding`](enum.Binding.md) for the given key press.

# `iced::widget::text_editor`

Text editors display a multi-line text input for text editing.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text_editor;

struct State {
   content: text_editor::Content,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    Edit(text_editor::Action)
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    text_editor(&state.content)
        .placeholder("Type something here...")
        .on_action(Message::Edit)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::Edit(action) => {
            state.content.perform(action);
        }
    }
}
```

- [`Content`](struct.Content.md) — The content of a [`TextEditor`](../struct.TextEditor.md).

# `iced::widget::text_input`

Text inputs display fields that can be filled with text.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text_input;

struct State {
   content: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    ContentChanged(String)
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    text_input("Type something here...", &state.content)
        .on_input(Message::ContentChanged)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::ContentChanged(content) => {
            state.content = content;
        }
    }
}
```

# `iced::widget::toggler`

Togglers let users make binary choices by toggling a switch.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::toggler;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    TogglerToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    toggler(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::TogglerToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::TogglerToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of a toggler.
- [`Toggler`](struct.Toggler.md) — A toggler widget.

## Traits

# `iced::widget::tooltip`

Tooltips display a hint of information over some element when hovered.

By default, the tooltip is displayed immediately, however, this can be adjusted with [`Tooltip::delay`](../struct.Tooltip.md).

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{container, tooltip};

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    tooltip(
        "Hover me to display the tooltip!",
        container("This is the tooltip contents!")
            .padding(10)
            .style(container::rounded_box),
        tooltip::Position::Bottom,
    )
}
```

## Structs

- [`Tooltip`](struct.Tooltip.md) — An element to display a widget over another.

## Enums

- [`Position`](enum.Position.md) — The position of the tooltip. Defaults to following the cursor.

# `iced::widget::vertical_slider`

Sliders let users set a value by moving an indicator.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::slider;

struct State {
   value: f32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    ValueChanged(f32),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    slider(0.0..=100.0, state.value, Message::ValueChanged)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::ValueChanged(value) => {
            state.value = value;
        }
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`Handle`](struct.Handle.md) — The appearance of the handle of a slider.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of a slider.
- [`VerticalSlider`](struct.VerticalSlider.md) — An vertical bar and a handle that selects a single value from a range of values.

## Enums

- [`HandleShape`](enum.HandleShape.md) — The shape of the handle of a slider.
- [`Status`](enum.Status.md) — The possible status of a [`Slider`](../struct.Slider.md).

## Traits

## Functions

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::HandleError`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum HandleError {
    NotSupported,
    Unavailable,
}
```

An error that can occur while fetching a display or window handle.

## Variants

### `NotSupported`

The underlying handle cannot be represented using the types in this crate.

This may be returned if the underlying window system does not support any of the representative C window handles in this crate. For instance, if you were using a pure Rust library to set up X11 (like [`x11rb`](https://crates.io/crates/x11rb)), you would not be able to use any of the [`RawWindowHandle`](enum.RawWindowHandle.md) variants, as they all represent C types.

Another example would be a system that isn’t supported by `raw-window-handle` yet, like some game consoles.

In the event that this error is returned, you should try to use the underlying window system’s native API to get the handle you need.

### `Unavailable`

The underlying handle is not available.

In some cases the underlying window handle may become temporarily unusable. For example, on Android, the native window pointer can arbitrarily be replaced or removed by the system. In this case, returning a window handle would be disingenuous, as it would not be usable. A similar situation can occur on Wayland for the layer shell windows.

In the event that this error is returned, you should wait until the handle becomes available again.

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::RawDisplayHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum RawDisplayHandle {
Show 13 variants    UiKit(UiKitDisplayHandle),
    AppKit(AppKitDisplayHandle),
    Orbital(OrbitalDisplayHandle),
    Ohos(OhosDisplayHandle),
    Xlib(XlibDisplayHandle),
    Xcb(XcbDisplayHandle),
    Wayland(WaylandDisplayHandle),
    Drm(DrmDisplayHandle),
    Gbm(GbmDisplayHandle),
    Windows(WindowsDisplayHandle),
    Web(WebDisplayHandle),
    Android(AndroidDisplayHandle),
    Haiku(HaikuDisplayHandle),
}
```

A display server handle for a particular windowing system.

The display usually represents a connection to some display server, but it is not necessarily tied to a particular window. Some APIs can use the display handle without ever creating a window handle (e.g. offscreen rendering, headless event handling).

Each variant contains a struct with fields specific to that windowing system (e.g. [`XlibDisplayHandle`](struct.XlibDisplayHandle.md) contains a [Display](https://www.x.org/releases/current/doc/libX11/libX11/libX11.html#Display_Functions) connection to an X Server, [`WaylandDisplayHandle`](struct.WaylandDisplayHandle.md) uses [wl_display](https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/html/apb.html#Client-classwl__display) to connect to a compositor). Not all windowing systems have a separate display handle (or they haven’t been implemented yet) and their variants contain empty structs.

## Variant Availability

Note that all variants are present on all targets (none are disabled behind `#[cfg]`s), but see the “Availability Hints” section on each variant for some hints on where this variant might be expected.

Note that these “Availability Hints” are not normative. That is to say, a [`HasDisplayHandle`](trait.HasDisplayHandle.md) implementor is completely allowed to return something unexpected. (For example, it’s legal for someone to return a [`RawDisplayHandle::Xlib`](enum.RawDisplayHandle.md) on macOS, it would just be weird, and probably requires something like XQuartz be used).

## Variants

### `UiKit(UiKitDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for UIKit (Apple’s non-macOS windowing library).

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to be used on iOS, tvOS, (in theory) watchOS, and Mac Catalyst (`$arch-apple-ios-macabi` targets, which can notably use UIKit *or* AppKit), as these are the targets that (currently) support UIKit.

### `AppKit(AppKitDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for AppKit.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to be used on macOS, although Mac Catalyst (`$arch-apple-ios-macabi` targets, which can notably use UIKit *or* AppKit) can also use it despite being `target_os = "ios"`.

### `Orbital(OrbitalDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for the Redox operating system.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used by the Orbital Windowing System in the Redox operating system.

### `Ohos(OhosDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for OpenHarmony OS NDK

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on OpenHarmony OS (`target_env = "ohos"`).

### `Xlib(XlibDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for Xlib.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to show up anywhere someone manages to get X11 working that Xlib can be built for, which is to say, most (but not all) Unix systems.

### `Xcb(XcbDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for Xcb.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to show up anywhere someone manages to get X11 working that XCB can be built for, which is to say, most (but not all) Unix systems.

### `Wayland(WaylandDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for Wayland.

###### Availability Hints

This variant should be expected anywhere Wayland works, which is currently some subset of unix systems.

### `Drm(DrmDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for the Linux Kernel Mode Set/Direct Rendering Manager

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Linux when neither X nor Wayland are available

### `Gbm(GbmDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for the Linux Generic Buffer Manager.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is present regardless of windowing backend and likely to be used with EGL_MESA_platform_gbm or EGL_KHR_platform_gbm.

### `Windows(WindowsDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for Win32.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Windows systems.

### `Web(WebDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for the Web.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Wasm or asm.js targets when targeting the Web/HTML5.

### `Android(AndroidDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for Android NDK.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Android targets.

### `Haiku(HaikuDisplayHandle)`

A raw display handle for Haiku.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on HaikuOS.

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::RawWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum RawWindowHandle {
Show 16 variants    UiKit(UiKitWindowHandle),
    AppKit(AppKitWindowHandle),
    Orbital(OrbitalWindowHandle),
    OhosNdk(OhosNdkWindowHandle),
    Xlib(XlibWindowHandle),
    Xcb(XcbWindowHandle),
    Wayland(WaylandWindowHandle),
    Drm(DrmWindowHandle),
    Gbm(GbmWindowHandle),
    Win32(Win32WindowHandle),
    WinRt(WinRtWindowHandle),
    Web(WebWindowHandle),
    WebCanvas(WebCanvasWindowHandle),
    WebOffscreenCanvas(WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle),
    AndroidNdk(AndroidNdkWindowHandle),
    Haiku(HaikuWindowHandle),
}
```

A window handle for a particular windowing system.

Each variant contains a struct with fields specific to that windowing system (e.g. [`Win32WindowHandle`](struct.Win32WindowHandle.md) will include a [HWND](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/about-windows#window-handle), [`WaylandWindowHandle`](struct.WaylandWindowHandle.md) uses [wl_surface](https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/html/apa.html#protocol-spec-wl_surface), etc.)

## Variant Availability

Note that all variants are present on all targets (none are disabled behind `#[cfg]`s), but see the “Availability Hints” section on each variant for some hints on where this variant might be expected.

Note that these “Availability Hints” are not normative. That is to say, a [`HasWindowHandle`](trait.HasWindowHandle.md) implementor is completely allowed to return something unexpected. (For example, it’s legal for someone to return a [`RawWindowHandle::Xlib`](enum.RawWindowHandle.md) on macOS, it would just be weird, and probably requires something like XQuartz be used).

## Variants

### `UiKit(UiKitWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for UIKit (Apple’s non-macOS windowing library).

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to be used on iOS, tvOS, (in theory) watchOS, and Mac Catalyst (`$arch-apple-ios-macabi` targets, which can notably use UIKit *or* AppKit), as these are the targets that (currently) support UIKit.

### `AppKit(AppKitWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for AppKit.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to be used on macOS, although Mac Catalyst (`$arch-apple-ios-macabi` targets, which can notably use UIKit *or* AppKit) can also use it despite being `target_os = "ios"`.

### `Orbital(OrbitalWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for the Redox operating system.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used by the Orbital Windowing System in the Redox operating system.

### `OhosNdk(OhosNdkWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for the OpenHarmony OS NDK

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on OpenHarmony OS (`target_env = "ohos"`).

### `Xlib(XlibWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for Xlib.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to show up anywhere someone manages to get X11 working that Xlib can be built for, which is to say, most (but not all) Unix systems.

### `Xcb(XcbWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for Xcb.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is likely to show up anywhere someone manages to get X11 working that XCB can be built for, which is to say, most (but not all) Unix systems.

### `Wayland(WaylandWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for Wayland.

###### Availability Hints

This variant should be expected anywhere Wayland works, which is currently some subset of unix systems.

### `Drm(DrmWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for the Linux Kernel Mode Set/Direct Rendering Manager

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Linux when neither X nor Wayland are available

### `Gbm(GbmWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for the Linux Generic Buffer Manager.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is present regardless of windowing backend and likely to be used with EGL_MESA_platform_gbm or EGL_KHR_platform_gbm.

### `Win32(Win32WindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for Win32.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Windows systems.

### `WinRt(WinRtWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for WinRT.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Windows systems.

### `Web(WebWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for the Web.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Wasm or asm.js targets when targeting the Web/HTML5.

### `WebCanvas(WebCanvasWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for a Web canvas registered via [`wasm-bindgen`](https://crates.io/crates/wasm-bindgen).

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Wasm or asm.js targets when targeting the Web/HTML5.

### `WebOffscreenCanvas(WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for a Web offscreen canvas registered via [`wasm-bindgen`](https://crates.io/crates/wasm-bindgen).

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Wasm or asm.js targets when targeting the Web/HTML5.

### `AndroidNdk(AndroidNdkWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for Android NDK.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on Android targets.

### `Haiku(HaikuWindowHandle)`

A raw window handle for Haiku.

###### Availability Hints

This variant is used on HaikuOS.

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle`

Interoperability library for Rust Windowing applications.

This library provides standard types for accessing a window’s platform-specific raw window handle and platforms display handle. This does not provide any utilities for creating and managing windows; instead, it provides a common interface that window creation libraries (e.g. Winit, SDL) can use to easily talk with graphics libraries (e.g. gfx-hal).

### Safety guarantees

Please see the docs of [`HasWindowHandle`](trait.HasWindowHandle.md) and [`HasDisplayHandle`](trait.HasDisplayHandle.md).

### Platform handle initialization

Each platform handle struct is purposefully non-exhaustive, so that additional fields may be added without breaking backwards compatibility. Each struct provides an `empty` method that may be used along with the struct update syntax to construct it. See each specific struct for examples.

### Display Handles

Some windowing systems use a separate display handle for some operations. The display usually represents a connection to some display server, but it is not necessarily tied to a particular window. See [`RawDisplayHandle`](enum.RawDisplayHandle.md) for more details.

## Structs

- [`AndroidDisplayHandle`](struct.AndroidDisplayHandle.md) — Raw display handle for Android.
- [`AndroidNdkWindowHandle`](struct.AndroidNdkWindowHandle.md) — Raw window handle for Android NDK.
- [`AppKitDisplayHandle`](struct.AppKitDisplayHandle.md) — Raw display handle for AppKit.
- [`AppKitWindowHandle`](struct.AppKitWindowHandle.md) — Raw window handle for AppKit.
- [`DisplayHandle`](struct.DisplayHandle.md) — The handle to the display controller of the windowing system.

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::AppKitWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct AppKitWindowHandle {
    pub ns_view: NonNull<c_void>,
}
```

Raw window handle for AppKit.

Note that `NSView` can only be accessed from the main thread of the application. This struct is `!Send` and `!Sync` to help with ensuring that.

## Example

Getting the view from a [`WindowHandle`](struct.WindowHandle.md).

```rust
#![cfg(target_os = "macos")]
use objc2_app_kit::NSView;
use objc2_foundation::is_main_thread;
use objc2::rc::Id;
use raw_window_handle::{WindowHandle, RawWindowHandle};

let handle: WindowHandle<'_>; // Get the window handle from somewhere else
match handle.as_raw() {
    RawWindowHandle::AppKit(handle) => {
        assert!(is_main_thread(), "can only access AppKit handles on the main thread");
        let ns_view = handle.ns_view.as_ptr();
        // SAFETY: The pointer came from `WindowHandle`, which ensures
        // that the `AppKitWindowHandle` contains a valid pointer to an
        // `NSView`.
        // Unwrap is fine, since the pointer came from `NonNull`.
        let ns_view: Id<NSView> = unsafe { Id::retain(ns_view.cast()) }.unwrap();
        // Do something with the NSView here, like getting the `NSWindow`
        let ns_window = ns_view.window().expect("view was not installed in a window");
    }
    handle => unreachable!("unknown handle {handle:?} for platform"),
}
```

## Fields

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::DisplayHandle`

```rust
pub struct DisplayHandle<'a> { /* private fields */ }
```

The handle to the display controller of the windowing system.

This is the primary return type of the [`HasDisplayHandle`](trait.HasDisplayHandle.md) trait. It is guaranteed to contain a valid platform-specific display handle for its lifetime.

## Methods

### `impl DisplayHandle<'static>`

#### `android`

```rust
pub fn android() -> DisplayHandle<'static>
```

Create an Android-based display handle.

As no data is borrowed by this handle, it is completely safe to create. This function may be useful to windowing framework implementations that want to avoid unsafe code.

###### Example

```rust
let handle = DisplayHandle::android();
do_something(handle);
```

### `impl DisplayHandle<'static>`

#### `appkit`

```rust
pub fn appkit() -> DisplayHandle<'static>
```

Create an AppKit-based display handle.

As no data is borrowed by this handle, it is completely safe to create. This function may be useful to windowing framework implementations that want to avoid unsafe code.

###### Example

```rust
let handle = DisplayHandle::appkit();
do_something(handle);
```

### `impl<'a> DisplayHandle<'a>`

#### `borrow_raw`

```rust
pub unsafe fn borrow_raw(raw: RawDisplayHandle) -> DisplayHandle<'a>
```

Create a `DisplayHandle` from a [`RawDisplayHandle`](enum.RawDisplayHandle.md).

###### Safety

Users can safely assume that non-`null`/`0` fields are valid handles, and it is up to the implementer of this trait to ensure that condition is upheld.

Despite that qualification, implementors should still make a best-effort attempt to fill in all available fields. If an implementation doesn’t, and a downstream user needs the field, it should try to derive the field from other fields the implementer *does* provide via whatever methods the platform provides.

It is not possible to invalidate a [`DisplayHandle`](struct.DisplayHandle.md) on any platform without additional unsafe code.

#### `as_raw`

```rust
pub fn as_raw(&self) -> RawDisplayHandle
```

Get the underlying raw display handle.

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::DrmDisplayHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct DrmDisplayHandle {
    pub fd: i32,
}
```

Raw display handle for the Linux Kernel Mode Set/Direct Rendering Manager.

## Fields

### `fd: i32`

The drm file descriptor.

## Methods

### `impl DrmDisplayHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(fd: i32) -> DrmDisplayHandle
```

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct DrmWindowHandle {
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::OhosNdkWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct OhosNdkWindowHandle {
    pub native_window: NonNull<c_void>,
}
```

Raw window handle for Ohos NDK.

## Fields

### `native_window: NonNull<c_void>`

## Methods

### `impl OhosNdkWindowHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(native_window: NonNull<c_void>) -> OhosNdkWindowHandle
```

Create a new handle to an [`OHNativeWindow`](https://gitee.com/openharmony/docs/blob/master/en/application-dev/reference/apis-arkgraphics2d/_native_window.md) on OpenHarmony.

The handle will typically be created from an [`XComponent`](https://gitee.com/openharmony/docs/blob/master/en/application-dev/ui/arkts-common-components-xcomponent.md), consult the [native `XComponent` Guidelines](https://gitee.com/openharmony/docs/blob/OpenHarmony-4.0-Release/en/application-dev/napi/xcomponent-guidelines.md) for more details.

###### Example

```rust
/// Called When the `XComponent` is created.
///
/// See the [XComponent Guidelines](https://gitee.com/openharmony/docs/blob/OpenHarmony-4.0-Release/en/application-dev/napi/xcomponent-guidelines.md)
/// for more details
extern "C" fn on_surface_created_callback(component: *mut OH_NativeXComponent, window: *mut c_void) {
    let handle = OhosNdkWindowHandle::new(NonNull::new(window).unwrap());
}
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::UiKitWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct UiKitWindowHandle {
    pub ui_view: NonNull<c_void>,
    pub ui_view_controller: Option<NonNull<c_void>>,
}
```

Raw window handle for UIKit.

Note that `UIView` can only be accessed from the main thread of the application. This struct is `!Send` and `!Sync` to help with ensuring that.

## Example

Getting the view from a [`WindowHandle`](struct.WindowHandle.md).

```rust
#![cfg(any(target_os = "ios", target_os = "tvos", target_os = "watchos", target_os = "xros"))]
use objc2_foundation::is_main_thread;
use objc2::rc::Id;
use objc2_ui_kit::UIView;
use raw_window_handle::{WindowHandle, RawWindowHandle};

let handle: WindowHandle<'_>; // Get the window handle from somewhere else
match handle.as_raw() {
    RawWindowHandle::UIKit(handle) => {
        assert!(is_main_thread(), "can only access UIKit handles on the main thread");
        let ui_view = handle.ui_view.as_ptr();
        // SAFETY: The pointer came from `WindowHandle`, which ensures
        // that the `UiKitWindowHandle` contains a valid pointer to an
        // `UIView`.
        // Unwrap is fine, since the pointer came from `NonNull`.
        let ui_view: Id<UIView> = unsafe { Id::retain(ui_view.cast()) }.unwrap();
        // Do something with the UIView here.
    }
    handle => unreachable!("unknown handle {handle:?} for platform"),
}
```

## Fields

### `ui_view: NonNull<c_void>`

A pointer to an `UIView` object.

### `ui_view_controller: Option<NonNull<c_void>>`

A pointer to an `UIViewController` object, if the view has one.

## Methods

### `impl UiKitWindowHandle`

#### `new`

```rust

```

Create a new handle to a view.

###### Example

```rust

// Optionally set the view controller.

```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::WebCanvasWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct WebCanvasWindowHandle {
    pub obj: NonNull<c_void>,
}
```

Raw window handle for a Web canvas registered via [`wasm-bindgen`](https://crates.io/crates/wasm-bindgen).

## Fields

### `obj: NonNull<c_void>`

A pointer to the [`JsValue`](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/latest/wasm_bindgen/struct.JsValue.html) of an [`HtmlCanvasElement`](https://docs.rs/web-sys/latest/web_sys/struct.HtmlCanvasElement.html).

Note: This uses [`c_void`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ffi/enum.c_void.html) to avoid depending on `wasm-bindgen` directly.

## Methods

### `impl WebCanvasWindowHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(obj: NonNull<c_void>) -> WebCanvasWindowHandle
```

Create a new handle from a pointer to [`HtmlCanvasElement`](https://docs.rs/web-sys/latest/web_sys/struct.HtmlCanvasElement.html).

###### Example

```rust
let canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement;
let value: &JsValue = &canvas; // Deref to `JsValue`
let obj: NonNull<c_void> = NonNull::from(value).cast();
let mut handle = WebCanvasWindowHandle::new(obj);
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle {
    pub obj: NonNull<c_void>,
}
```

Raw window handle for a Web offscreen canvas registered via [`wasm-bindgen`](https://crates.io/crates/wasm-bindgen).

## Fields

### `obj: NonNull<c_void>`

A pointer to the [`JsValue`](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/latest/wasm_bindgen/struct.JsValue.html) of an [`OffscreenCanvas`](https://docs.rs/web-sys/latest/web_sys/struct.OffscreenCanvas.html).

Note: This uses [`c_void`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ffi/enum.c_void.html) to avoid depending on `wasm-bindgen` directly.

## Methods

### `impl WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(obj: NonNull<c_void>) -> WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle
```

Create a new handle from a pointer to an [`OffscreenCanvas`](https://docs.rs/web-sys/latest/web_sys/struct.OffscreenCanvas.html).

###### Example

```rust
let canvas: &OffscreenCanvas;
let value: &JsValue = &canvas; // Deref to `JsValue`
let obj: NonNull<c_void> = NonNull::from(value).cast();
let mut handle = WebOffscreenCanvasWindowHandle::new(obj);
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::WebWindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct WebWindowHandle {
    pub id: u32,
}
```

Raw window handle for the Web.

## Fields

### `id: u32`

An ID value inserted into the [data attributes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/data-*) of the canvas element as ‘`raw-handle`’.

When accessing from JS, the attribute will automatically be called `rawHandle`.

Each canvas created by the windowing system should be assigned their own unique ID.

## Methods

### `impl WebWindowHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(id: u32) -> WebWindowHandle
```

Create a new handle to a canvas element.

###### Example

```rust
let id: u32 = 0; // canvas.rawHandle;
let handle = WebWindowHandle::new(id);
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::Win32WindowHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct Win32WindowHandle {
    pub hwnd: NonZero<isize>,
    pub hinstance: Option<NonZero<isize>>,
}
```

Raw window handle for Win32.

## Fields

### `hwnd: NonZero<isize>`

A Win32 `HWND` handle.

### `hinstance: Option<NonZero<isize>>`

The `GWLP_HINSTANCE` associated with this type’s `HWND`.

## Methods

### `impl Win32WindowHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(hwnd: NonZero<isize>) -> Win32WindowHandle
```

Create a new handle to a window.

###### Safety

It is assumed that the Win32 handle belongs to the current thread. This is necessary for the handle to be considered “valid” in all cases.

###### Example

```rust
let window: HWND;
let mut handle = Win32WindowHandle::new(NonZeroIsize::new(window.0).unwrap());
// Optionally set the GWLP_HINSTANCE.
let hinstance = NonZeroIsize::new(unsafe { GetWindowLongPtrW(window, GWLP_HINSTANCE) }).unwrap();
handle.hinstance = hinstance;
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::WindowHandle`

```rust
pub struct WindowHandle<'a> { /* private fields */ }
```

The handle to a window.

This is the primary return type of the [`HasWindowHandle`](trait.HasWindowHandle.md) trait. All *pointers* within this type are guaranteed to be valid and not dangling for the lifetime of the handle. This excludes window IDs like XIDs and the window ID for web platforms. See the documentation on the [`HasWindowHandle`](trait.HasWindowHandle.md) trait for more information about these safety requirements.

This handle is guaranteed to be safe and valid.

## Methods

### `impl<'a> WindowHandle<'a>`

#### `borrow_raw`

```rust
pub unsafe fn borrow_raw(raw: RawWindowHandle) -> WindowHandle<'a>
```

Borrow a `WindowHandle` from a [`RawWindowHandle`](enum.RawWindowHandle.md).

###### Safety

Users can safely assume that non-`null`/`0` fields are valid handles, and it is up to the implementer of this trait to ensure that condition is upheld.

Despite that qualification, implementers should still make a best-effort attempt to fill in all available fields. If an implementation doesn’t, and a downstream user needs the field, it should try to derive the field from other fields the implementer *does* provide via whatever methods the platform provides.

Note that this guarantee only applies to *pointers*, and not any window ID types in the handle. This includes Window IDs (XIDs) from X11 and the window ID for web platforms. There is no way for Rust to enforce any kind of invariant on these types, since:

- For all three listed platforms, it is possible for safe code in the same process to delete the window.
- For X11, it is possible for code in a different process to delete the window. In fact, it is possible for code on a different *machine* to delete the window.

It is *also* possible for the window to be replaced with another, valid-but-different window. User code should be aware of this possibility, and should be ready to soundly handle the possible error conditions that can arise from this.

#### `as_raw`

```rust
pub fn as_raw(&self) -> RawWindowHandle
```

Get the underlying raw window handle.

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::XcbDisplayHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct XcbDisplayHandle {
    pub connection: Option<NonNull<c_void>>,
    pub screen: i32,
}
```

Raw display handle for Xcb.

## Fields

### `connection: Option<NonNull<c_void>>`

A pointer to an X server `xcb_connection_t`.

It is strongly recommended to set this value, however it may be set to `None` to request the default display when using EGL.

### `screen: i32`

An X11 screen to use with this display handle.

Note, that X11 could have multiple screens, however graphics APIs could work only with one screen at the time, given that multiple screens usually reside on different GPUs.

## Methods

### `impl XcbDisplayHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(connection: Option<NonNull<c_void>>, screen: i32) -> XcbDisplayHandle
```

Create a new handle to a connection and screen.

###### Example

```rust
let connection: NonNull<c_void>;
let screen;
let handle = XcbDisplayHandle::new(Some(connection), screen);
```

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::XlibDisplayHandle`

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct XlibDisplayHandle {
    pub display: Option<NonNull<c_void>>,
    pub screen: i32,
}
```

Raw display handle for Xlib.

## Fields

### `display: Option<NonNull<c_void>>`

A pointer to an Xlib `Display`.

It is strongly recommended to set this value, however it may be set to `None` to request the default display when using EGL.

### `screen: i32`

An X11 screen to use with this display handle.

Note, that X11 could have multiple screens, however graphics APIs could work only with one screen at the time, given that multiple screens usually reside on different GPUs.

## Methods

### `impl XlibDisplayHandle`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(display: Option<NonNull<c_void>>, screen: i32) -> XlibDisplayHandle
```

Create a new handle to a display.

###### Example

```rust
let display: NonNull<c_void>;
let screen;
let handle = XlibDisplayHandle::new(Some(display), screen);
```

---

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::HasDisplayHandle`

```rust
pub trait HasDisplayHandle {
    // Required method
    fn display_handle(&self) -> Result<DisplayHandle<'_>, HandleError>;
}
```

A display that acts as a wrapper around a display handle.

Objects that implement this trait should be able to return a [`DisplayHandle`](struct.DisplayHandle.md) for the display that they are associated with. This handle should last for the lifetime of the object, and should return an error if the application is inactive.

Implementors of this trait will be windowing systems, like [`winit`](https://crates.io/crates/winit) and [`sdl2`](https://crates.io/crates/sdl2). These windowing systems should implement this trait on types that represent the top-level display server. It should be implemented by tying the lifetime of the [`DisplayHandle`](struct.DisplayHandle.md) to the lifetime of the display object.

Users of this trait will include graphics libraries, like [`wgpu`](https://crates.io/crates/wgpu) and [`glutin`](https://crates.io/crates/glutin). These APIs should be generic over a type that implements `HasDisplayHandle`, and should use the [`DisplayHandle`](struct.DisplayHandle.md) type to access the display handle.

Note that these requirements are not enforced on `HasDisplayHandle`, rather, they are enforced on the constructors of [`DisplayHandle`](struct.DisplayHandle.md). This is because the `HasDisplayHandle` trait is safe to implement.

## Required Methods

### `display_handle`

```rust
fn display_handle(&self) -> Result<DisplayHandle<'_>, HandleError>
```

Get a handle to the display controller of the windowing system.

## Implementors

- `impl HasDisplayHandle for Headless`
- `impl<'a> HasDisplayHandle for DisplayHandle<'a>`

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::HasRawDisplayHandle`

```rust
pub unsafe trait HasRawDisplayHandle {
    // Required method
    fn raw_display_handle(&self) -> Result<RawDisplayHandle, HandleError>;
}
```

Display that wraps around a raw display handle.

## Safety

Users can safely assume that pointers and non-zero fields are valid, and it is up to the implementer of this trait to ensure that condition is upheld.

Despite that qualification, implementers should still make a best-effort attempt to fill in all available fields. If an implementation doesn’t, and a downstream user needs the field, it should try to derive the field from other fields the implementer *does* provide via whatever methods the platform provides.

The exact handles returned by `raw_display_handle` must remain consistent between multiple calls to `raw_display_handle` as long as not indicated otherwise by platform specific events.

## Required Methods

### `raw_display_handle`

```rust
fn raw_display_handle(&self) -> Result<RawDisplayHandle, HandleError>
```

*👎Deprecated: Use HasDisplayHandle instead*

## Implementors

- `impl<T> HasRawDisplayHandle for T where T: HasDisplayHandle + ?Sized,`

# `iced::window::raw_window_handle::HasWindowHandle`

```rust
pub trait HasWindowHandle {
    // Required method
    fn window_handle(&self) -> Result<WindowHandle<'_>, HandleError>;
}
```

A handle to a window.

Objects that implement this trait should be able to return a [`WindowHandle`](struct.WindowHandle.md) for the window that they are associated with. This handle should last for the lifetime of the object, and should return an error if the application is inactive.

Implementors of this trait will be windowing systems, like [`winit`](https://crates.io/crates/winit) and [`sdl2`](https://crates.io/crates/sdl2). These windowing systems should implement this trait on types that represent windows.

Users of this trait will include graphics libraries, like [`wgpu`](https://crates.io/crates/wgpu) and [`glutin`](https://crates.io/crates/glutin). These APIs should be generic over a type that implements `HasWindowHandle`, and should use the [`WindowHandle`](struct.WindowHandle.md) type to access the window handle. The window handle should be acquired and held while the window is being used, in order to ensure that the window is not deleted while it is in use.

## Required Methods

### `window_handle`

```rust
fn window_handle(&self) -> Result<WindowHandle<'_>, HandleError>
```

Get a handle to the window.

## Implementors

- `impl HasWindowHandle for Headless`
- `impl HasWindowHandle for WindowHandle<'_>`

# `iced::advanced::widget::operation`

Query or update internal widget state.

## Modules

- [`focusable`](focusable/index.md) — Operate on widgets that can be focused.
- [`scrollable`](scrollable/index.md) — Operate on widgets that can be scrolled.
- [`text`](text/index.md) — Operate on widgets that have text.
- [`text_input`](text_input/index.md) — Operate on widgets that have text input.

## Enums

- [`Animation`](enum.Animation.md) — The animation to apply to a state change, as requested by an [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md).
- [`Outcome`](enum.Outcome.md) — The result of an [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md).

## Traits

- [`Focusable`](trait.Focusable.md) — The internal state of a widget that can be focused.
- [`Operation`](trait.Operation.md) — A piece of logic that can traverse the widget tree of an application in order to query or update some widget state.
- [`Scrollable`](trait.Scrollable.md) — The internal state of a widget that can be scrolled.
- [`Text`](trait.Text.md) — The internal state of a widget that has text.
- [`TextInput`](trait.TextInput.md) — The internal state of a widget that has text input.

## Functions

- [`black_box`](fn.black_box.md) — Wraps the [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md) in a black box, erasing its returning type.
- [`map`](fn.map.md) — Maps the output of an [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md) using the given function.
- [`scope`](fn.scope.md) — Produces an [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md) that applies the given [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md) to the children of a container with the given [`Id`](../../../widget/struct.Id.md).
- [`then`](fn.then.md) — Chains the output of an [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md) with the provided function to build a new [`Operation`](../trait.Operation.md).

# `iced::advanced::widget::operation::Text`

```rust
pub trait Text {
    // Required methods
    fn text(&self) -> Cow<'_, str>;
    fn select(&mut self, start: Point, end: Point, target: Target);
    fn select_all(&mut self);
    fn deselect(&mut self);
    fn copy(&mut self) -> Option<String>;
}
```

The internal state of a widget that has text.

## Required Methods

### `text`

```rust
fn text(&self) -> Cow<'_, str>
```

Returns the text of the widget.

### `select`

```rust
fn select(&mut self, start: Point, end: Point, target: Target)
```

Selects text between the given positions in layout coordinates.

`start` is the position where the user started selecting from, while `end` is the final position of the selection.

### `select_all`

```rust
fn select_all(&mut self)
```

Selects all the text of the widget.

### `deselect`

```rust
fn deselect(&mut self)
```

Deselects any selected text;

### `copy`

```rust
fn copy(&mut self) -> Option<String>
```

Returns the selected text, if any.

# `iced::advanced::widget::operation::TextInput`

```rust
pub trait TextInput {
    // Required methods
    fn text(&self) -> Cow<'_, str>;
    fn move_cursor_to_front(&mut self);
    fn move_cursor_to_end(&mut self);
    fn move_cursor_to(&mut self, location: Position);
    fn select_all(&mut self);
    fn select_range(&mut self, start: Position, end: Position);
}
```

The internal state of a widget that has text input.

## Required Methods

### `text`

```rust
fn text(&self) -> Cow<'_, str>
```

Returns the current *visible* text of the text input.

Normally, this is either its value or its placeholder.

### `move_cursor_to_front`

```rust
fn move_cursor_to_front(&mut self)
```

Moves the cursor of the text input to the front of the input text.

### `move_cursor_to_end`

```rust
fn move_cursor_to_end(&mut self)
```

Moves the cursor of the text input to the end of the input text.

### `move_cursor_to`

```rust
fn move_cursor_to(&mut self, location: Position)
```

Moves the cursor of the text input to an arbitrary location.

### `select_all`

```rust
fn select_all(&mut self)
```

Selects all the content of the text input.

### `select_range`

```rust
fn select_range(&mut self, start: Position, end: Position)
```

Selects the given content range of the text input.

## Implementors

- `impl<R> TextInput for Input<R> where R: Renderer,`
- `impl<T> TextInput for T where T: Editor,`

# `iced::advanced::widget::text`

Text widgets display information through writing.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text;
use iced::color;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    text("Hello, this is iced!")
        .size(20)
        .color(color!(0x0000ff))
}
```

## Structs

- [`Format`](struct.Format.md) — The format of some [`Text`](../struct.Text.md).
- [`Operand`](struct.Operand.md) — The state of a widget with text, operated on by [`super::Operation::text`](../trait.Operation.md).
- [`Position`](struct.Position.md) — A specific position in some [`Text`](../../struct.Text.md).
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of some text.
- [`Text`](struct.Text.md) — A bunch of text.

## Enums

- [`Alignment`](enum.Alignment.md) — The alignment of some text.
- [`Ellipsis`](enum.Ellipsis.md) — The ellipsis strategy of some text.
- [`LineHeight`](enum.LineHeight.md) — The height of a line of text in a paragraph.
- [`Shaping`](enum.Shaping.md) — The shaping strategy of some text.
- [`Wrapping`](enum.Wrapping.md) — The wrapping strategy of some text.

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`Text`](../struct.Text.md).

## Functions

- [`base`](fn.base.md) — Text with the default base color.
- [`danger`](fn.danger.md) — Text conveying some negative information, like an error.
- [`default`](fn.default.md) — The default text styling; color is inherited.
- [`draw`](fn.draw.md) — Draws text using the same logic as the [`Text`](../struct.Text.md) widget.
- [`layout`](fn.layout.md) — Computes the [`Size`](../../../struct.Size.md) of a [`Text`](../struct.Text.md) widget.
- [`primary`](fn.primary.md) — Text conveying some important information, like an action.
- [`secondary`](fn.secondary.md) — Text conveying some secondary information, like a footnote.
- [`success`](fn.success.md) — Text conveying some positive information, like a successful event.
- [`warning`](fn.warning.md) — Text conveying some mildly negative information, like a warning.

## Type Aliases

- [`StyleFn`](type.StyleFn.md) — A styling function for a [`Text`](../struct.Text.md).

# `iced::widget::canvas::path::lyon_path`

Data structures and traits to work with paths (vector graphics).

To build and consume paths, see the [builder](builder/index.md) and [iterator](iterator/index.md) modules.

This crate is reexported in [lyon](https://docs.rs/lyon/).

## Examples

```rust
use lyon_path::Path;
use lyon_path::math::{point};
use lyon_path::builder::*;

// Create a builder object to build the path.
let mut builder = Path::builder();

// Build a simple path.
let mut builder = Path::builder();
builder.begin(point(0.0, 0.0));
builder.line_to(point(1.0, 2.0));
builder.line_to(point(2.0, 0.0));
builder.line_to(point(1.0, 1.0));
builder.close();

// Generate the actual path object.
let path = builder.build();

for event in &path {
    println!("{:?}", event);
}
```

# `iced::widget::canvas::path::lyon_path::builder`

Path building utilities.

### `PathBuilder` or `SvgPathBuilder`

Path can be built via either of two abstractions:

- [PathBuilder](trait.PathBuilder.md) is a simple and efficient interface which does not deal with any ambiguous cases.
- [SvgPathBuilder](trait.SvgPathBuilder.md) is a higher-level interface that follows SVG’s specification, removing the the burden of dealing with special cases from the user at a run-time cost.

`SvgPathBuilder` may be a better choice when interactive with SVG, or dealing with arbitrary input. `PathBuilder`. `PathBuilder` is probably a more useful trait to implement when creating a new path data structure since all `PathBuilder` implementations automatically get an `SvgPathBuilder` adapter (see the `with_svg` method). It may also make sense to use the `PathBuilder` API when following a specification that behaves like SVG paths or when no performance can be traded for convenience.

### Examples

The following example shows how to create a simple path using the [PathBuilder](trait.PathBuilder.md) interface.

```rust
use lyon_path::{Path, geom::point};

let mut builder = Path::builder();

// All sub-paths *must* have be contained in a begin/end pair.
builder.begin(point(0.0, 0.0));
builder.line_to(point(1.0, 0.0));
builder.quadratic_bezier_to(point(2.0, 0.0), point(2.0, 1.0));
builder.end(false);

builder.begin(point(10.0, 0.0));
builder.cubic_bezier_to(point(12.0, 2.0), point(11.0, 2.0), point(5.0, 0.0));
builder.close(); // close() is equivalent to end(true).

let path = builder.build();
```

The same path can be built using the `SvgPathBuilder` API:

```rust
use lyon_path::{Path, geom::{point, vector}, builder::SvgPathBuilder};

// Use the SVG adapter.
let mut builder = Path::builder().with_svg();

// All sub-paths *must* have be contained in a begin/end pair.
builder.move_to(point(0.0, 0.0));
builder.line_to(point(1.0, 0.0));
builder.quadratic_bezier_to(point(2.0, 0.0), point(2.0, 1.0));
// No need to explicitly end a sub-path.

builder.move_to(point(10.0, 0.0));
builder.relative_cubic_bezier_to(vector(2.0, 2.0), vector(1.0, 2.0), vector(-5.0, 0.0));
builder.close();

let path = builder.build();
```

Implementors of the `PathBuilder` trait automatically gain access to a few other adapters. For example a builder that approximates curves with a sequence of line segments:

```rust
use lyon_path::{Path, geom::point};

let tolerance = 0.05;// maximum distance between a curve and its approximation.
let mut builder = Path::builder().flattened(tolerance);

builder.begin(point(0.0, 0.0));
builder.quadratic_bezier_to(point(1.0, 0.0), point(1.0, 1.0));
builder.end(true);

// The resulting path contains only Begin, Line and End events.
let path = builder.build();
```

## Structs

- [`BorderRadii`](struct.BorderRadii.md) — The radius of each corner of a rounded rectangle.
- [`Flattened`](struct.Flattened.md) — A Builder that approximates curves with successions of line segments.
- [`NoAttributes`](struct.NoAttributes.md) — A convenience wrapper for `PathBuilder` without custom attributes.
- [`Transformed`](struct.Transformed.md) — Builds a path with a transformation applied.
- [`WithSvg`](struct.WithSvg.md) — Implements an SVG-like building interface on top of a PathBuilder.
