# `iced_test::ice::Ice`

```rust
pub struct Ice {
    pub viewport: Size,
    pub mode: Mode,
    pub preset: Option<String>,
    pub instructions: Vec<Instruction>,
}
```

An end-to-end test for iced applications.

Ice tests encode a certain configuration together with a sequence of instructions. An ice test passes if all the instructions can be executed successfully.

Normally, ice tests are run by an [`Emulator`](../emulator/struct.Emulator.md) in continuous integration pipelines.

Ice tests can be easily run by saving them as `.ice` files in a folder and simply calling [`run`](../fn.run.md). These test files can be recorded by enabling the `tester` feature flag in the root crate.

**Source:** [ice.rs](../../src/iced_test/ice.rs.md) (lines 19-28)

## Fields

### `viewport: Size`

The viewport [`Size`] that must be used for the test.

### `mode: Mode`

The [`emulator::Mode`](../emulator/enum.Mode.md) that must be used for the test.

### `preset: Option<String>`

The name of the `Preset` that must be used for the test.

### `instructions: Vec<Instruction>`

The sequence of instructions of the test.

## Methods

### `impl Ice`

#### `parse`

```rust
pub fn parse(content: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>
```

Parses an [`Ice`](struct.Ice.md) test from its textual representation.

Here is an example of the [`Ice`](struct.Ice.md) test syntax:

```
viewport: 500x800
mode: Immediate
preset: Empty
-----
click "What needs to be done?"
type "Create the universe"
type enter
type "Make an apple pie"
type enter
expect "2 tasks left"
click "Create the universe"
expect "1 task left"
click "Make an apple pie"
expect "0 tasks left"
```

This syntax is *very* experimental and extremely likely to change often. For this reason, it is reserved for advanced users that want to early test it.

Currently, in order to use it, you will need to earn the right and prove you understand its experimental nature by reading the code!

```rust
pub enum Expectation {
```

# `iced_test::instruction::Instruction`

```rust
pub enum Instruction {
    Interact(Interaction),
    Expect(Expectation),
}
```

A step in an end-to-end test.

An [`Instruction`](enum.Instruction.md) can be run by an [`Emulator`](../emulator/struct.Emulator.md).

**Source:** [instruction.rs](../../src/iced_test/instruction.rs.md) (lines 13-18)

### `Interact(Interaction)`

# `iced_test::instruction::Interaction`

```rust
pub enum Interaction {
    Mouse(Mouse),
    Keyboard(Keyboard),
}
```

A user interaction.

**Source:** [instruction.rs](../../src/iced_test/instruction.rs.md) (lines 38-43)

## Variants

### `Mouse(Mouse)`

A mouse interaction.

### `Keyboard(Keyboard)`

A keyboard interaction.

## Methods

### `impl Interaction`

#### `from_event`

```rust
pub fn from_event(event: &Event) -> Option<Self>
```

Creates an [`Interaction`](enum.Interaction.md) from a runtime [`Event`].

This can be useful for recording tests during real usage.

#### `merge`

```rust
pub fn merge(self, next: Self) -> (Self, Option<Self>)
```

Merges two interactions together, if possible.

This method can turn certain sequences of interactions into a single one. For instance, a mouse movement, left button press, and left button release can all be merged into a single click interaction.

Merging is lossy and, therefore, it is not always desirable if you are recording a test and want full reproducibility.

If the interactions cannot be merged, the `next` interaction will be returned as the second element of the tuple.

#### `events`

```rust
pub fn events( &self, find_target: impl FnOnce(&Target) -> Option<Point>, ) -> Option<Vec<Event>>
```

Returns a list of runtime events representing the [`Interaction`](enum.Interaction.md).

The `find_target` closure must convert a [`Target`](enum.Target.md) into its screen coordinates.

# `iced_test::simulator`

Run a simulation of your application without side effects.

## Structs

- [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md) — A user interface that can be interacted with and inspected programmatically.
- [`Snapshot`](struct.Snapshot.md) — A frame of a user interface rendered by a [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

## Functions

- [`click`](fn.click.md) — Returns the sequence of events of a click.
- [`press_key`](fn.press_key.md) — Returns the sequence of events of a key press.
- [`release_key`](fn.release_key.md) — Returns the sequence of events of a key release.
- [`scroll`](fn.scroll.md) — Returns the sequence of events of a scroll, with the given `delta`.
- [`simulator`](fn.simulator.md) — Creates a new [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).
- [`tap_key`](fn.tap_key.md) — Returns the sequence of events of a “key tap” (i.e. pressing and releasing a key).
- [`typewrite`](fn.typewrite.md) — Returns the sequence of events of typewriting the given text in a keyboard.



```rust

```

Finds the target of the given widget [`Selector`](../trait.Selector.md) in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

#### `point_at`

```rust
pub fn point_at(&mut self, position: impl Into<Point>)
```

Points the mouse cursor at the given position in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

This does *not* produce mouse movement events!

#### `operate`

```rust
pub fn operate(&mut self, operation: &mut dyn Operation)
```

Applies a [`widget::Operation`] to the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md)’s widget tree.

#### `rebuild`

```rust
pub fn rebuild( self, element: impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a, ) -> Self
```

Rebuilds the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md)’s user interface with a new `element`, preserving the state of widgets with an unchanged id.

#### `resize`

```rust
pub fn resize(self, size: impl Into<Size>) -> Self
```

Resizes the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md)’s window to the given `size`, relaying out the user interface and preserving widget state.

#### `click`

```rust
pub fn click<S>(&mut self, selector: S) -> Result<S::Output, Error> where S: Selector + Send, S::Output: Bounded + Clone + Send + Sync + 'static,
```

Clicks the [`Bounded`] target found by the given [`Selector`](../trait.Selector.md), if any.

This consists in:

- Pointing the mouse cursor at the center of the [`Bounded`] target.
- Simulating a [`click`](fn.click.md).

#### `tap_key`

```rust
pub fn tap_key(&mut self, key: impl Into<Key>) -> Status
```

Simulates a key press, followed by a release, in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

#### `typewrite`

```rust
pub fn typewrite(&mut self, text: &str) -> Status
```

Simulates a user typing in the keyboard the given text in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

#### `scroll`

```rust
pub fn scroll(&mut self, delta: ScrollDelta) -> Status
```

Scrolls with the given `delta` in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

The mouse cursor must be over the content being scrolled for the scroll to be applied, e.g. via [`Self::point_at`](struct.Simulator.md).

#### `simulate`

```rust
pub fn simulate( &mut self, events: impl IntoIterator<Item = Event>, ) -> Vec<Status>
```

Simulates the given raw sequence of events in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

#### `draw`

```rust
pub fn draw(&mut self, theme: &Theme)
```

Draws the interface in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md) with the given theme.

A `RedrawRequested` event is processed before drawing.

#### `snapshot`

```rust
pub fn snapshot(&mut self, theme: &Theme) -> Result<Snapshot, Error>
```

Draws and takes a [`Snapshot`](struct.Snapshot.md) of the interface in the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

#### `into_messages`

```rust
pub fn into_messages( self, ) -> impl Iterator<Item = Message> + use<Message, Theme, Renderer>
```

Turns the [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md) into the sequence of messages produced by any interactions.

#### `drain`

```rust
pub fn drain(&mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Message>
```

Returns the messages published so far, clearing the queue.

# `iced_test::simulator::Snapshot`

```rust
pub struct Snapshot { /* private fields */ }
```

A frame of a user interface rendered by a [`Simulator`](struct.Simulator.md).

**Source:** [simulator.rs](../../src/iced_test/simulator.rs.md) (lines 295-298)

## Methods

### `impl Snapshot`

#### `matches_image`

```rust
pub fn matches_image(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<bool, Error>
```

Compares the [`Snapshot`](struct.Snapshot.md) with the PNG image found in the given path, returning `true` if they are identical.

If the PNG image does not exist, it will be created by the [`Snapshot`](struct.Snapshot.md) for future testing and `true` will be returned.

#### `matches_hash`

```rust
pub fn matches_hash(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<bool, Error>
```

Compares the [`Snapshot`](struct.Snapshot.md) with the SHA-256 hash file found in the given path, returning `true` if they are identical.

If the hash file does not exist, it will be created by the [`Snapshot`](struct.Snapshot.md) for future testing and `true` will be returned.

# `iced_wgpu`

A [`wgpu`](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu-rs) renderer for [Iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced).

![The native path of the Iced ecosystem](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced/blob/0525d76ff94e828b7b21634fa94a747022001c83/docs/graphs/native.png?raw=true)

[`wgpu`](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu-rs) supports most modern graphics backends: Vulkan, Metal, DX11, and DX12 (OpenGL and WebGL are still WIP). Additionally, it will support the incoming [WebGPU API](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/).

Currently, `iced_wgpu` supports the following primitives:

- Text, which is rendered using [`glyphon`](https://github.com/grovesNL/glyphon).
- Quads or rectangles, with rounded borders and a solid background color.
- Clip areas, useful to implement scrollables or hide overflowing content.
- Images and SVG, loaded from memory or the file system.
- Meshes of triangles, useful to draw geometry freely.

## Re-exports

- [`Layer`](layer/struct.Layer.md)
- [`Primitive`](primitive/trait.Primitive.md)
- [`Geometry`](geometry/enum.Geometry.md) *(geometry)*
- `pub use iced_graphics as graphics;`
- `pub use iced_graphics::core;`
- `pub use wgpu;`

## Modules

- [`geometry`](geometry/index.md) *(geometry)* — Build and draw geometry.
- [`layer`](layer/index.md)
- [`primitive`](primitive/index.md) — Draw custom primitives.
- [`window`](window/index.md) — Display rendering results on windows.

## Structs

- [`Engine`](struct.Engine.md)
- [`Renderer`](struct.Renderer.md) — A [`wgpu`](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu-rs) graphics renderer for [`iced`](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced).

# `iced_wgpu::Renderer`

```rust
pub struct Renderer { /* private fields */ }
```

A [`wgpu`](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu-rs) graphics renderer for [`iced`](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced).

**Source:** [lib.rs](../src/iced_wgpu/lib.rs.md) (lines 73-93)

## Methods

### `impl Renderer`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new(engine: Engine, settings: Settings) -> Self
```

#### `draw`

```rust
pub fn draw( &mut self, clear_color: Option<Color>, target: &TextureView, viewport: &Viewport, ) -> CommandEncoder
```

Record commands that draw the current primitives to the target texture view.

You must call [`finish`](struct.Renderer.md) and [`recall`](struct.Renderer.md) when submitting the resulting [`wgpu::CommandEncoder`].

#### `present`

```rust
pub fn present( &mut self, clear_color: Option<Color>, _format: TextureFormat, frame: &TextureView, viewport: &Viewport, ) -> SubmissionIndex
```

#### `screenshot`

```rust
pub fn screenshot( &mut self, viewport: &Viewport, background_color: Color, ) -> Vec<u8> ⓘ
```

Renders the current surface to an offscreen buffer.

Returns RGBA bytes of the texture data.

#### `finish`

```rust
pub fn finish(&mut self)
```

Prepares currently mapped buffers for use in a submission.

Usually, this method is only needed if you are calling [`Renderer::draw`](struct.Renderer.md) directly, instead of relying on [`Renderer::present`](struct.Renderer.md).

You must call this method *before* submitting the resulting [`wgpu::CommandEncoder`] of [`Renderer::draw`](struct.Renderer.md) to a [`wgpu::Queue`].

#### `recall`

```rust
pub fn recall(&mut self)
```

Recalls all of the closed buffers back to be reused.

Usually, this method is only needed if you are calling [`Renderer::draw`](struct.Renderer.md) directly, instead of relying on [`Renderer::present`](struct.Renderer.md) to a [`wgpu::Queue`].

You must call this method *after* submitting the resulting [`wgpu::CommandEncoder`] of [`Renderer::draw`](struct.Renderer.md) to a [`wgpu::Queue`].

# `iced_wgpu::primitive`

Draw custom primitives.

## Structs

- [`Instance`](struct.Instance.md) — An instance of a specific [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md).
- [`Storage`](struct.Storage.md) — Stores custom, user-provided types.

## Traits

- [`Pipeline`](trait.Pipeline.md) — The pipeline of a graphics [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md).
- [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md) — A set of methods which allows a [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md) to be rendered.
- [`Renderer`](trait.Renderer.md) — A renderer than can draw custom primitives.

## Type Aliases

- [`Batch`](type.Batch.md) — A batch of primitives.

# `iced_wgpu::primitive::Pipeline`

```rust
pub trait Pipeline:
    Any
    + MaybeSend
    + MaybeSync {
    // Required method
    fn new(device: &Device, queue: &Queue, format: TextureFormat) -> Self
       where Self: Sized;

    // Provided method
    fn trim(&mut self) { ... }
}
```

The pipeline of a graphics [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md).

**Source:** [primitive.rs](../../src/iced_wgpu/primitive.rs.md) (lines 67-80)

## Required Methods

### `new`

```rust
fn new(device: &Device, queue: &Queue, format: TextureFormat) -> Self where Self: Sized,
```

Creates the [`Pipeline`](trait.Pipeline.md) of a [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md).

This will only be called once, when the first [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md) with this kind of [`Pipeline`](trait.Pipeline.md) is encountered.

## Provided Methods

### `trim`

```rust
fn trim(&mut self)
```

Trims any cached data in the [`Pipeline`](trait.Pipeline.md).

This will normally be called at the end of a frame.

# `iced_wgpu::primitive::Primitive`

```rust
pub trait Primitive:
    Debug
    + MaybeSend
    + MaybeSync
    + 'static {
    type Pipeline: Pipeline + MaybeSend + MaybeSync;

    // Required method
    fn prepare(
        &self,
        pipeline: &mut Self::Pipeline,
        device: &Device,
        queue: &Queue,
        bounds: &Rectangle,
        viewport: &Viewport,
    );

    // Provided methods
    fn draw(
        &self,
        _pipeline: &Self::Pipeline,
        _render_pass: &mut RenderPass<'_>,
    ) -> bool { ... }
    fn render(
        &self,
        _pipeline: &Self::Pipeline,
        _encoder: &mut CommandEncoder,
        _target: &TextureView,
        _clip_bounds: &Rectangle<u32>,
    ) { ... }
}
```

A set of methods which allows a [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md) to be rendered.

**Source:** [primitive.rs](../../src/iced_wgpu/primitive.rs.md) (lines 14-64)

## Required Associated Types

### `Pipeline`

```rust
type Pipeline: Pipeline + MaybeSend + MaybeSync
```

The shared renderer of this [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md).

Normally, this will contain a bunch of [`wgpu`] state; like a rendering pipeline, buffers, and textures.

All instances of this [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md) type will share the same [`Renderer`](trait.Renderer.md).

## Required Methods

### `prepare`

```rust
fn prepare( &self, pipeline: &mut Self::Pipeline, device: &Device, queue: &Queue, bounds: &Rectangle, viewport: &Viewport, )
```

Processes the [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md), allowing for GPU buffer allocation.

## Provided Methods

### `draw`

```rust
fn draw( &self, _pipeline: &Self::Pipeline, _render_pass: &mut RenderPass<'_>, ) -> bool
```

Draws the [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md) in the given [`wgpu::RenderPass`].

When possible, this should be implemented over [`render`](trait.Primitive.md) since reusing the existing render pass should be considerably more efficient than issuing a new one.

The viewport and scissor rect of the render pass provided is set to the bounds and clip bounds of the [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md), respectively.

If you have complex composition needs, then you can leverage [`render`](trait.Primitive.md) by returning `false` here.

By default, it does nothing and returns `false`.

### `render`

```rust
fn render( &self, _pipeline: &Self::Pipeline, _encoder: &mut CommandEncoder, _target: &TextureView, _clip_bounds: &Rectangle<u32>, )
```

Renders the [`Primitive`](trait.Primitive.md), using the given [`wgpu::CommandEncoder`].

This will only be called if [`draw`](trait.Primitive.md) returns `false`.

By default, it does nothing.

## Implementors

# `iced_wgpu::window::Surface`

```rust
pub struct Surface<'window> { /* private fields */ }
```

Handle to a presentable surface.

A `Surface` represents a platform-specific surface (e.g. a window) onto which rendered images may be presented. A `Surface` may be created with the function [`Instance::create_surface`].

This type is unique to the Rust API of `wgpu`. In the WebGPU specification, [`GPUCanvasContext`](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#canvas-context) serves a similar role.

## Methods

### `impl Surface<'_>`

#### `get_capabilities`

```rust
pub fn get_capabilities(&self, adapter: &Adapter) -> SurfaceCapabilities
```

Returns the capabilities of the surface when used with the given adapter.

Returns specified values (see [`SurfaceCapabilities`]) if surface is incompatible with the adapter.

#### `display_hdr_info`

```rust
pub fn display_hdr_info(&self, adapter: &Adapter) -> DisplayHdrInfo
```

Returns the HDR and luminance characteristics of the display backing this surface, or [`DisplayHdrInfo::default`] (all fields `None`) when nothing is known - which means unknown, not an SDR display. Never panics, including on wasm. See [`DisplayHdrInfo`] for the fields and how to use them.

###### Threading

Each call re-queries the OS; nothing is cached. On the Metal backend the display’s HDR state lives on main-thread-only AppKit objects (`NSScreen` / `NSWindow`), so call this from the main thread. Off the main thread it logs once and returns [`DisplayHdrInfo::default`]; a later main-thread call still returns real data. No other backend has this requirement.

#### `get_default_config`

```rust
pub fn get_default_config( &self, adapter: &Adapter, width: u32, height: u32, ) -> Option<SurfaceConfiguration<Vec<TextureFormat>>>
```

Return a default `SurfaceConfiguration` from width and height to use for the [`Surface`](struct.Surface.md) with this adapter.

The returned configuration requests the surface’s preferred format and [`SurfaceColorSpace::Auto`], reproducing wgpu’s historical SDR / standard behavior. Set the `color_space` field to opt into wide-gamut or HDR output; see [`SurfaceColorSpace`] for what each color space means.

Returns None if the surface isn’t supported by this adapter

#### `configure`

```rust
pub fn configure( &self, device: &Device, config: &SurfaceConfiguration<Vec<TextureFormat>>, )
```

Initializes [`Surface`](struct.Surface.md) for presentation.

If the surface is already configured, this will wait for the GPU to come idle before recreating the swapchain to prevent race conditions.

###### Validation Errors

- Submissions that happen *during* the configure may cause the internal wait-for-idle to fail, raising a validation error.

###### Panics

- An old [`SurfaceTexture`] is still alive referencing an old surface.
- Texture format requested is unsupported on the surface.
- The requested color space is unsupported for the requested format (see [`SurfaceCapabilities::format_capabilities`]).
- `config.width` or `config.height` is zero.

#### `get_configuration`

```rust
pub fn get_configuration( &self, ) -> Option<SurfaceConfiguration<Vec<TextureFormat>>>
```

Returns the current configuration of [`Surface`](struct.Surface.md), if configured.

This is similar to [WebGPU `GPUcCanvasContext::getConfiguration`](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#dom-gpucanvascontext-getconfiguration).

Note that this returns the configuration as passed to [`Surface::configure`](struct.Surface.md): automatic values such as [`SurfaceColorSpace::Auto`] are returned as-is, not as the concrete values they resolved to.

#### `get_current_texture`

```rust
pub fn get_current_texture(&self) -> CurrentSurfaceTexture
```

Returns the next texture to be presented by the surface for drawing.

After rendering to the returned [`SurfaceTexture`], submit work via [`Queue::submit`] and then call [`Queue::present`] to display it.

If a [`SurfaceTexture`] referencing this surface is alive when [`Surface::configure()`](struct.Surface.md) is called, the configure call will panic.

See the documentation of [`CurrentSurfaceTexture`] for how each possible result should be handled.

#### `as_hal`

```rust
pub unsafe fn as_hal<A>( &self, ) -> Option<impl Deref<Target = <A as Api>::Surface> + WasmNotSendSync> where A: Api,
```

*Available on wgpu_core only.*

Get the [`wgpu_hal`] surface from this `Surface`.

Find the Api struct corresponding to the active backend in [`wgpu_hal::api`], and pass that struct to the to the `A` type parameter.

Returns a guard that dereferences to the type of the hal backend which implements `A::Surface`.

###### Types

The returned type depends on the backend:

- [`hal::api::Vulkan`] uses [`hal::vulkan::Surface`]
- `hal::api::Metal` uses `hal::metal::Surface`
- `hal::api::Dx12` uses `hal::dx12::Surface`
- [`hal::api::Gles`] uses [`hal::gles::Surface`]

###### Errors

This method will return None if:

- The surface is not from the backend specified by `A`.
- The surface is from the `webgpu` or `custom` backend.

###### Safety

- The returned resource must not be destroyed unless the guard is the last reference to it and it is not in use by the GPU. The guard and handle may be dropped at any time however.
- All the safety requirements of wgpu-hal must be upheld.

# `iced_wgpu::window::compositor::Error`

```rust
pub enum Error {
    SurfaceCreationFailed(CreateSurfaceError),
    IncompatibleSurface,
    NoAdapterFound(String),
    RequestDeviceFailed(Vec<(Limits, RequestDeviceError)>),
}
```

A compositor error.

**Source:** [compositor.rs](../../../src/iced_wgpu/window/compositor.rs.md) (lines 22-35)

## Variants

### `SurfaceCreationFailed(CreateSurfaceError)`

The surface creation failed.

### `IncompatibleSurface`

# `iced_wgpu::window::compositor::present_mode_from_env`

```rust
pub fn present_mode_from_env() -> Option<PresentMode>
```

Obtains a [`wgpu::PresentMode`] from the current environment configuration, if set.

The value returned by this function can be changed by setting the `ICED_PRESENT_MODE` env variable. The possible values are:

- `vsync` → [`wgpu::PresentMode::AutoVsync`]
- `no_vsync` → [`wgpu::PresentMode::AutoNoVsync`]
- `immediate` → [`wgpu::PresentMode::Immediate`]
- `fifo` → [`wgpu::PresentMode::Fifo`]
- `fifo_relaxed` → [`wgpu::PresentMode::FifoRelaxed`]
- `mailbox` → [`wgpu::PresentMode::Mailbox`]

**Source:** [compositor.rs](../../../src/iced_wgpu/window/compositor.rs.md) (lines 446-458)

# `iced_wgpu::window::compositor`

Connect a window with a renderer.

## Structs

- [`Compositor`](struct.Compositor.md) — A window graphics backend for iced powered by `wgpu`.
- [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md) — The settings of a [`Compositor`](struct.Compositor.md).

## Enums

- [`Error`](enum.Error.md) — A compositor error.

## Functions

- [`new`](fn.new.md) — Creates a [`Compositor`](struct.Compositor.md) with the given [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md) and window.
- [`present`](fn.present.md) — Presents the given primitives with the given [`Compositor`](struct.Compositor.md).
- [`present_mode_from_env`](fn.present_mode_from_env.md) — Obtains a [`wgpu::PresentMode`] from the current environment configuration, if set.

```rust
pub struct Settings {
    pub present_mode: PresentMode,

}
```

**Source:** [compositor.rs](../../../src/iced_wgpu/window/compositor.rs.md) (lines 375-393)

## Fields

### `backends: Backends`

The graphics backends to use.

### `power_preference: PowerPreference`

The power-usage preference for graphics adapters.

By default, it is [`backend::PowerPreference::None`].

### `antialiasing: Option<Antialiasing>`

The antialiasing strategy that will be used for triangle primitives.

By default, it is `None`.


### `impl<ST, DT> CastableFrom<ST, Initialized, Initialized> for DT where ST: ?Sized, DT: ?Sized,`

### `impl<ST, DT> CastableFrom<ST, Uninit, Uninit> for DT where ST: ?Sized, DT: ?Sized,`

### `impl<T> MaybeSend for T where T: Send,`

### `impl<T> MaybeSync for T where T: Sync,`

### `impl<T> Read<Exclusive, BecauseExclusive> for T where T: ?Sized,`

### `impl<T> WasmNotSend for T where T: Send,`

### `impl<T> WasmNotSendSync for T where T: WasmNotSend + WasmNotSync,`

### `impl<T> WasmNotSync for T where T: Sync,`

# `iced_widget::canvas`

```rust
pub fn canvas<P, Message, Theme, Renderer>(
    program: P,
) -> Canvas<P, Message, Theme, Renderer> where
    Renderer: Renderer,
    P: Program<Message, Theme, Renderer>,
```

Creates a new [`Canvas`](canvas/struct.Canvas.md).

Canvases can be leveraged to draw interactive 2D graphics.

## Example: Drawing a Simple Circle

```rust
use iced::mouse;
use iced::widget::canvas;
use iced::{Color, Rectangle, Renderer, Theme};

// First, we define the data we need for drawing
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Circle {
    radius: f32,
}

// Then, we implement the `Program` trait
impl<Message> canvas::Program<Message> for Circle {
    // No internal state
    type State = ();

    fn draw(
        &self,
        _state: &(),
        renderer: &Renderer,
        _theme: &Theme,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: mouse::Cursor
    ) -> Vec<canvas::Geometry> {
        // We prepare a new `Frame`
        let mut frame = canvas::Frame::new(renderer, bounds.size());

        // We create a `Path` representing a simple circle
        let circle = canvas::Path::circle(frame.center(), self.radius);

        // And fill it with some color
        frame.fill(&circle, Color::BLACK);

        // Then, we produce the geometry
        vec![frame.into_geometry()]
    }
}

// Finally, we simply use our `Circle` to create the `Canvas`!
fn view<Message>(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    canvas(Circle { radius: 50.0 })
}
```

**Source:** [helpers.rs](../src/iced_widget/helpers.rs.md) (lines 1602-1608)

# `iced_widget::checkbox`

```rust
pub fn checkbox<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer>(
    is_checked: bool,
) -> Checkbox<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer> where
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
    Renderer: Renderer,
```

Creates a new [`Checkbox`](checkbox/struct.Checkbox.md).

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::checkbox;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    CheckboxToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    checkbox(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::CheckboxToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::CheckboxToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

# `iced_widget::combo_box`

```rust
pub fn combo_box<'a, T, Message, Theme>(
    state: &'a State<T>,
    placeholder: impl IntoFragment<'a>,
    selection: Option<&T>,
    on_selected: impl Fn(T) -> Message + 'a,
) -> ComboBox<'a, T, Message, Theme> where
    T: Display + Clone,
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
```

Creates a new [`ComboBox`](combo_box/struct.ComboBox.md).

Combo boxes display a dropdown list of searchable and selectable options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::combo_box;

struct State {
   fruits: combo_box::State<Fruit>,
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    combo_box(
        &state.fruits,
        "Select your favorite fruit...",
        state.favorite.as_ref(),
        Message::FruitSelected
    )
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

# `iced_widget::markdown`

```rust
pub fn markdown<'a, Theme, Renderer>(
    items: &'a [Item],
    settings: impl Into<Settings>,
    theme: Theme,
) -> impl Widget<Uri, Theme, Renderer> + 'awhere
    Theme: Catalog + 'static,
    Renderer: Renderer,
```

Display a bunch of Markdown items.

You can obtain the items with [`parse`](markdown/fn.parse.md).

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::markdown;
use iced::{Theme, Widget};

struct State {
   markdown: Vec<markdown::Item>,
}

enum Message {
    LinkClicked(markdown::Uri),
}

impl State {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            markdown: markdown::parse("This is some **Markdown**!").collect(),
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message> {
        markdown::view(
            &self.markdown,
            markdown::Settings::default(),
            Theme::TokyoNight,
        )
            .map(Message::LinkClicked)
    }

    fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::LinkClicked(url) => {
                println!("The following url was clicked: {url}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# `iced_widget::opaque`

```rust
pub fn opaque<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer>(
    content: impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a,
) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'awhere
    Message: 'a,
    Theme: 'a,
    Renderer: Renderer + 'a,
```

Wraps the given widget and captures any mouse button presses inside the bounds of the widget—effectively making it *opaque*.

This helper is meant to be used to mark elements in a `Stack` to avoid mouse events from passing through layers.

# `iced_widget::pane_grid`

```rust
pub fn pane_grid<'a, T, Message, Title, W, Theme, Renderer>(
    state: &'a State<T>,
    view: impl Fn(Pane, &'a T, bool) -> Content<'a, Message, Title, W, Theme, Renderer>,
) -> PaneGrid<'a, Message, Title, W, Theme, Renderer> where
    Theme: Catalog,
    Renderer: Renderer,
```

Creates a [`PaneGrid`](pane_grid/struct.PaneGrid.md) with the given [`pane_grid::State`](pane_grid/state/struct.State.md) and view function.

Pane grids let your users split regions of your application and organize layout dynamically.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{pane_grid, text};

struct State {
    panes: pane_grid::State<Pane>,
}

enum Pane {
    SomePane,
    AnotherKindOfPane,
}

enum Message {
    PaneDragged(pane_grid::DragEvent),
    PaneResized(pane_grid::ResizeEvent),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    pane_grid(&state.panes, |pane, state, is_maximized| {
        pane_grid::Content::new(match state {
            Pane::SomePane => text("This is some pane"),
            Pane::AnotherKindOfPane => text("This is another kind of pane"),
        })
    })
    .on_drag(Message::PaneDragged)
    .on_resize(10, Message::PaneResized)
}
```

# `iced_widget::pick_list`

```rust
pub fn pick_list<'a, T, L, V, Message, Theme>(
    selected: Option<V>,
    options: L,
    to_string: impl Fn(&T) -> String + 'a,
) -> PickList<'a, T, L, V, Message, Theme> where
    T: PartialEq + Clone + 'a,
    L: Borrow<[T]> + 'a,
    V: Borrow<T> + 'a,
    Message: Clone,
    Theme: Catalog + Catalog,
```

Creates a new [`PickList`](pick_list/struct.PickList.md).

Pick lists display a dropdown list of selectable options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::pick_list;

struct State {
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let fruits = [
        Fruit::Apple,
        Fruit::Orange,
        Fruit::Strawberry,
        Fruit::Tomato,
    ];

    pick_list(
        state.favorite,
        fruits,
        Fruit::to_string,
    )
    .on_select(Message::FruitSelected)
    .placeholder("Select your favorite fruit...")
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

# `iced_widget::radio`

```rust
pub fn radio<'a, Message, Theme, V>(
    label: impl Into<String>,
    value: V,
    selected: Option<V>,
    on_click: impl FnOnce(V) -> Message,
) -> Radio<'a, Message, Theme> where
    Message: Clone,
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
    V: Copy + Eq,
```

Creates a new [`Radio`](radio/struct.Radio.md).

Radio buttons let users choose a single option from a bunch of options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::{column, radio};

struct State {
   selection: Option<Choice>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum Message {
    RadioSelected(Choice),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Choice {
    A,
    B,
    C,
    All,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let a = radio(
        "A",
        Choice::A,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let b = radio(
        "B",
        Choice::B,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let c = radio(
        "C",
        Choice::C,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected,
    );

    let all = radio(
        "All of the above",
        Choice::All,
        state.selection,
        Message::RadioSelected
    );

    column![a, b, c, all]
}
```

# `iced_widget::text_editor`

```rust
pub fn text_editor<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer>(
    content: &'a Content<Renderer>,
) -> TextEditor<'a, PlainText, Message, Theme, Renderer> where
    Message: Clone,
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
    Renderer: Renderer,
```

Creates a new [`TextEditor`](text_editor/struct.TextEditor.md).

Text editors display a multi-line text input for text editing.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text_editor;

struct State {
   content: text_editor::Content,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    Edit(text_editor::Action)
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    text_editor(&state.content)
        .placeholder("Type something here...")
        .on_action(Message::Edit)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::Edit(action) => {
            state.content.perform(action);
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
pub fn text_input<'a, Message, Theme>(
    placeholder: impl IntoFragment<'a>,
    value: impl IntoFragment<'a>,
) -> TextInput<'a, Message, Theme> where
    Message: Clone,
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
```

Text inputs display fields that can be filled with text.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::text_input;

struct State {
   content: String,
}

enum Message {
    ContentChanged(String)
}

    text_input("Type something here...", &state.content)

}

        Message::ContentChanged(content) => {
            state.content = content;
        }
    }
```

# `iced_widget::toggler`

```rust
pub fn toggler<'a, Message, Theme>(
    is_checked: bool,
) -> Toggler<'a, Message, Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
```

Creates a new [`Toggler`](toggler/struct.Toggler.md).

Togglers let users make binary choices by toggling a switch.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::toggler;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    TogglerToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    toggler(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::TogglerToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::TogglerToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

# `iced_widget::transition`

```rust
pub fn transition<'a, Message, W, P>(
    value: P::Value,
    init: impl Fn() -> P + 'a,
    view: impl Fn(&P, Instant) -> W + 'a,
) -> Transition<'a, Message, W, P> where
    P: Program,
```

Creates a new [`Transition`](transition/struct.Transition.md).

The `init` closure will be used to initialize an implementor of [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md). This is normally an `Animation`, but you can implement [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md) on your own types as well.

The `view` closure will receive the [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md) and the current [`Instant`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.Instant.html), which can be used for interpolating values. When the `value` changes, this will be called every frame, until the [`Program`](transition/trait.Program.md) stops animating.

## Example

Here is how you could implement a smooth progress bar:

```rust
use iced::widget::{transition, progress_bar};
use iced::Animation;

fn smooth_progress_bar<Message>(progress: f32) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    transition(progress, || Animation::new(0.).quick(), |animation, now| {
        progress_bar(0.0..=1.0, animation.interpolate_with(std::convert::identity, now))
    })
}
```

**Source:** [helpers.rs](../src/iced_widget/helpers.rs.md) (lines 1769-1778)

- [`Element`](type.Element.md) — A boxed [`Widget`](trait.Widget.md).

## Example

# `iced_widget::text`

```rust
macro_rules! text {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```

Creates a new `Text` widget with the provided content.

This macro uses the same syntax as [`format!`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html), but creates a new `Text` widget instead.

See [the formatting documentation in `std::fmt`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/fmt/index.html) for details of the macro argument syntax.

## Examples

```rust
use iced::widget::text;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    let simple = text!("Hello, world!");

    let keyword = text!("Hello, {}", "world!");

    let planet = "Earth";
    let local_variable = text!("Hello, {planet}!");
    // ...
}
```

**Source:** [helpers.rs](../src/iced_widget/helpers.rs.md) (lines 173-177)

# `iced_widget::Action`

```rust
pub struct Action<Message> { /* private fields */ }
```

A runtime action that can be performed by some widgets.

**Source:** [action.rs](../src/iced_widget/action.rs.md) (lines 7-11)

## Methods

### `impl<Message> Action<Message>`

#### `none`

```rust
pub fn none() -> Self
```

Creates an [`Action`](struct.Action.md) that does nothing.

#### `capture`

```rust
pub fn capture() -> Self
```

Creates a new “capturing” [`Action`](struct.Action.md). A capturing [`Action`](struct.Action.md) will make other widgets consider it final and prevent further processing.

Prevents “event bubbling”.

#### `publish`

```rust
pub fn publish(message: Message) -> Self
```

Creates a new [`Action`](struct.Action.md) that publishes the given `Message` for the application to handle.

Publishing a `Message` always produces a redraw.

#### `request_redraw`

```rust
pub fn request_redraw() -> Self
```

Creates a new [`Action`](struct.Action.md) that requests a redraw to happen as soon as possible; without publishing any `Message`.

#### `request_redraw_at`

```rust
pub fn request_redraw_at(at: Instant) -> Self
```

Creates a new [`Action`](struct.Action.md) that requests a redraw to happen at the given [`Instant`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.Instant.html); without publishing any `Message`.

This can be useful to efficiently animate content, like a blinking caret on a text input.

#### `and_capture`

```rust
pub fn and_capture(self) -> Self
```

Marks the [`Action`](struct.Action.md) as “capturing”. See [`Self::capture`](struct.Action.md).

#### `and_request_redraw_at`

```rust
pub fn and_request_redraw_at(self, at: Instant) -> Self
```

Requests a redraw at the given [`Instant`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.Instant.html). See [`Self::request_redraw_at`](struct.Action.md).

#### `into_inner`

```rust
pub fn into_inner(self) -> (Option<Message>, RedrawRequest, Status)
```

Converts the [`Action`](struct.Action.md) into its internal parts.

This method is meant to be used by runtimes, libraries, or internal widget implementations.

# `iced_widget::Widget`

```rust
pub trait Widget<Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer>: Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> {
    // Provided methods
    fn map<F, B>(self, f: F) -> Map<Self, F, Message>
       where Self: Sized,
             F: Fn(Message) -> B { ... }
    fn boxed<'a>(self) -> Element<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer>
       where Self: Sized + 'a { ... }
    fn explain(
        self,
        color: impl Into<Color>,
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer>
       where Self: Sized,
             Renderer: Renderer { ... }
}
```

A widget that can be rendered by iced.

This trait extends [`core::Widget`] with a few convenient methods—like [`Widget::map`](trait.Widget.md), [`Widget::boxed`](trait.Widget.md), and [`Widget::explain`](trait.Widget.md)—and defaults the `Theme` and `Renderer` parameters to iced’s.

**Source:** [lib.rs](../src/iced_widget/lib.rs.md) (lines 180-354)

## Provided Methods

### `map`

```rust
fn map<F, B>(self, f: F) -> Map<Self, F, Message> where Self: Sized, F: Fn(Message) -> B,
```

Applies a transformation to the produced message of this [`Widget`](trait.Widget.md).

This method is useful when you want to decouple different parts of your UI and make them **composable**.

###### Example

Imagine we want to use [our counter](index.md). But instead of showing a single counter, we want to display many of them. We can reuse the `Counter` type as it is!

We use composition to model the **state** of our new application:

```rust
use counter::Counter;

struct ManyCounters {
    counters: Vec<Counter>,
}
```

We can store the state of multiple counters now. However, the **messages** we implemented before describe the user interactions of a **single** counter. Right now, we need to also identify which counter is receiving user interactions. Can we use composition again? Yes.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Message {
    Counter(usize, counter::Message)
}
```

We compose the previous **messages** with the index of the counter producing them. Let’s implement our **view logic** now:

```rust
use counter::Counter;

use iced::widget::row;
use iced::{Function, Widget};

struct ManyCounters {
    counters: Vec<Counter>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Message {
    Counter(usize, counter::Message),
}

impl ManyCounters {
    pub fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message, iced_widget::Theme, ()> {
        // We can quickly populate a `row` by mapping our counters
        row(
            self.counters
                .iter()
                .map(Counter::view)
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(index, counter)| {
                    // Here we turn our `Element<counter::Message>` into
                    // an `Element<Message>` by combining the `index` and the
                    // message of the `element`.
                    counter.map(Message::Counter.with(index)).boxed()
                }),
        )
    }
}
```

Finally, our **update logic** is pretty straightforward: simple delegation.

```rust
impl ManyCounters {
    pub fn update(&mut self, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::Counter(index, counter_msg) => {
                if let Some(counter) = self.counters.get_mut(index) {
                    counter.update(counter_msg);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### `boxed`

```rust
fn boxed<'a>(self) -> Element<'a, Message, Theme, Renderer> where Self: Sized + 'a,
```

Boxes this [`Widget`](trait.Widget.md), turning it into a generic [`Element`](type.Element.md).

### `explain`

```rust
fn explain( self, color: impl Into<Color>, ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> where Self: Sized, Renderer: Renderer,
```

Marks this [`Widget`](trait.Widget.md) as *to-be-explained*.

The [`Renderer`](type.Renderer.md) will explain its layout graphically. This can be very useful for debugging your layout!

# `iced_widget::button::Status`

```rust
pub enum Status {
    Active,
    Hovered,
    Pressed,
    Disabled,
}
```

The possible status of a [`Button`](struct.Button.md).

**Source:** [button.rs](../../src/iced_widget/button.rs.md) (lines 453-462)

## Variants

### `Active`

The [`Button`](struct.Button.md) can be pressed.

### `Hovered`

The [`Button`](struct.Button.md) can be pressed and it is being hovered.

### `Pressed`

The [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is being pressed.

### `Disabled`

The [`Button`](struct.Button.md) cannot be pressed.

# `iced_widget::button`

Buttons allow your users to perform actions by pressing them.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::button;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    ButtonPressed,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    button("Press me!").on_press(Message::ButtonPressed)
}
```

## Structs

- [`Button`](struct.Button.md) — A generic widget that produces a message when pressed.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The style of a button.

## Enums

- [`Status`](enum.Status.md) — The possible status of a [`Button`](struct.Button.md).

## Constants

- [`DEFAULT_PADDING`](constant.DEFAULT_PADDING.md) — The default [`Padding`] of a [`Button`](struct.Button.md).

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`Button`](struct.Button.md).

## Functions

- [`background`](fn.background.md) — A button using background shades.
- [`danger`](fn.danger.md) — A danger button; denoting a destructive action.
- [`primary`](fn.primary.md) — A primary button; denoting a main action.
- [`secondary`](fn.secondary.md) — A secondary button; denoting a complementary action.
- [`subtle`](fn.subtle.md) — A subtle button using weak background shades.
- [`success`](fn.success.md) — A success button; denoting a good outcome.
- [`text`](fn.text.md) — A text button; useful for links.
- [`warning`](fn.warning.md) — A warning button; denoting a risky action.

## Type Aliases

- [`StyleFn`](type.StyleFn.md) — A styling function for a [`Button`](struct.Button.md).

# `iced_widget::button::Button`

```rust
pub struct Button<'a, Message, W = Element<'a, Message>, Theme = Theme> where
    Theme: Catalog, { /* private fields */ }
```

A generic widget that produces a message when pressed.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::button;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    ButtonPressed,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    button("Press me!").on_press(Message::ButtonPressed)
}
```

If a [`Button::on_press`](struct.Button.md) handler is not set, the resulting [`Button`](struct.Button.md) will be disabled:

```rust
use iced::widget::button;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Message {
    ButtonPressed,
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    button("I am disabled!")
}
```

**Source:** [button.rs](../../src/iced_widget/button.rs.md) (lines 71-83)

## Methods

### `impl<'a, Message, W, Theme> Button<'a, Message, W, Theme> where Theme: Catalog,`

```rust
pub fn new(content: W) -> Self
```

Creates a new [`Button`](struct.Button.md) with the given content.

#### `width`

#### `height`

```rust

```

#### `on_press`

```rust
pub fn on_press(self, on_press: Message) -> Self
```

Sets the message that will be produced when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is pressed.

Unless `on_press` is called, the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) will be disabled.

#### `on_press_with`

```rust
pub fn on_press_with(self, on_press: impl Fn() -> Message + 'a) -> Self
```

Sets the message that will be produced when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is pressed.

This is analogous to [`Button::on_press`](struct.Button.md), but using a closure to produce the message.

This closure will only be called when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is actually pressed and, therefore, this method is useful to reduce overhead if creating the resulting message is slow.

#### `on_press_maybe`

```rust
pub fn on_press_maybe(self, on_press: Option<Message>) -> Self
```

Sets the message that will be produced when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is pressed, if `Some`.

If `None`, the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) will be disabled.

#### `on_press_maybe_with`

```rust
pub fn on_press_maybe_with( self, on_press: Option<impl Fn() -> Message + 'a>, ) -> Self
```

Sets the message that will be produced when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is pressed, if `Some`.

This is analogous to [`Button::on_press`](struct.Button.md), but using a closure to produce the message.

This closure will only be called when the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) is actually pressed and, therefore, this method is useful to reduce overhead if creating the resulting message is slow.

If `None`, the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) will be disabled.

#### `clip`

```rust
pub fn clip(self, clip: bool) -> Self
```

Sets whether the contents of the [`Button`](struct.Button.md) should be clipped on overflow.

# `iced_widget::button::Catalog`

```rust
pub trait Catalog {
    type Class<'a>;

    // Required methods
    fn default<'a>() -> Self::Class<'a>;
    fn style(&self, class: &Self::Class<'_>, status: Status) -> Style;
}
```

The theme catalog of a [`Button`](struct.Button.md).

All themes that can be used with [`Button`](struct.Button.md) must implement this trait.

## Example

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub enum ButtonClass {
    #[default]
    Primary,
    Secondary,
    Danger
}

impl Catalog for MyTheme {
    type Class<'a> = ButtonClass;
    fn default<'a>() -> Self::Class<'a> {
        ButtonClass::default()
    }

    fn style(&self, class: &Self::Class<'_>, status: Status) -> Style {
        let mut style = Style::default();

        match class {
            ButtonClass::Primary => {
                style.background = Some(Background::Color(Color::from_rgb(0.529, 0.808, 0.921)));
            },
            ButtonClass::Secondary => {
                style.background = Some(Background::Color(Color::WHITE));
            },
            ButtonClass::Danger => {
                style.background = Some(Background::Color(Color::from_rgb(0.941, 0.502, 0.502)));
            },
        }

        style
    }
}
```

Although, in order to use [`Button::style`](struct.Button.md) with `MyTheme`, [`Catalog::Class`](trait.Catalog.md) must implement `From<StyleFn<'_, MyTheme>>`.

# `iced_widget::canvas`

Canvases can be leveraged to draw interactive 2D graphics.

## Example: Drawing a Simple Circle

```rust
use iced::mouse;
use iced::widget::canvas;
use iced::{Color, Rectangle, Renderer, Theme};

// First, we define the data we need for drawing
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Circle {
    radius: f32,
}

// Then, we implement the `Program` trait
impl<Message> canvas::Program<Message> for Circle {
    // No internal state
    type State = ();

    fn draw(
        &self,
        _state: &(),
        renderer: &Renderer,
        _theme: &Theme,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: mouse::Cursor
    ) -> Vec<canvas::Geometry> {
        // We prepare a new `Frame`
        let mut frame = canvas::Frame::new(renderer, bounds.size());

        // We create a `Path` representing a simple circle
        let circle = canvas::Path::circle(frame.center(), self.radius);

        // And fill it with some color
        frame.fill(&circle, Color::BLACK);

        // Then, we produce the geometry
        vec![frame.into_geometry()]
    }
}

// Finally, we simply use our `Circle` to create the `Canvas`!
fn view<Message>(_state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    canvas(Circle { radius: 50.0 })
}
```

## Re-exports

- [`Action`](../struct.Action.md)

## Modules

- [`fill`](fill/index.md) — Fill `Geometry` with a certain style.
- [`gradient`](gradient/index.md) — A gradient that can be used as a fill for some geometry.
- [`path`](path/index.md) — Build different kinds of 2D shapes.
- [`stroke`](stroke/index.md) — Create lines from a [`Path`](struct.Path.md) and assigns them various attributes/styles.

- [`Canvas`](struct.Canvas.md) — A widget capable of drawing 2D graphics.
- [`Fill`](struct.Fill.md) — The style used to fill geometry.
- [`Group`](struct.Group.md) — A cache group.
- [`Image`](struct.Image.md) — A raster image that can be drawn.
- [`LineDash`](struct.LineDash.md) — The dash pattern used when stroking the line.
- [`Path`](struct.Path.md) — An immutable set of points that may or may not be connected.
- [`Stroke`](struct.Stroke.md) — The style of a stroke.
- [`Text`](struct.Text.md) — A bunch of text that can be drawn to a canvas

## Enums

- [`LineJoin`](enum.LineJoin.md) — The shape used at the corners of paths or basic shapes when they are stroked.

# `iced_widget::canvas::Program`

```rust
pub trait Program<Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer> where
    Renderer: Renderer, {
    type State: Default + 'static;

    // Required method
    fn draw(
        &self,
        state: &Self::State,
        renderer: &Renderer,
        theme: &Theme,
        bounds: Rectangle,
        cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Vec<Geometry<Renderer>> ⓘ;

    // Provided methods
    fn update(
        &self,
        _state: &mut Self::State,
        _event: &Event,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Option<Action<Message>> { ... }
    fn mouse_interaction(
        &self,
        _state: &Self::State,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Interaction { ... }
}
```

The state and logic of a [`Canvas`](struct.Canvas.md).

A [`Program`](trait.Program.md) can mutate internal state and produce messages for an application.

**Source:** [program.rs](../../src/iced_widget/canvas/program.rs.md) (lines 13-73)

## Required Associated Types

### `State`

```rust
type State: Default + 'static
```

The internal state mutated by the [`Program`](trait.Program.md).

## Required Methods

### `draw`

```rust
fn draw( &self, state: &Self::State, renderer: &Renderer, theme: &Theme, bounds: Rectangle, cursor: Cursor, ) -> Vec<Geometry<Renderer>> ⓘ
```

Draws the state of the [`Program`](trait.Program.md), producing a bunch of [`Geometry`](type.Geometry.md).

[`Geometry`](type.Geometry.md) can be easily generated with a [`Frame`](type.Frame.md) or stored in a [`Cache`](type.Cache.md).

## Provided Methods

### `update`

```rust
fn update( &self, _state: &mut Self::State, _event: &Event, _bounds: Rectangle, _cursor: Cursor, ) -> Option<Action<Message>>
```

Updates the [`State`](trait.Program.md) of the [`Program`](trait.Program.md).

When a [`Program`](trait.Program.md) is used in a [`Canvas`](struct.Canvas.md), the runtime will call this method for each [`Event`](enum.Event.md).

This method can optionally return an [`Action`](../struct.Action.md) to either notify an application of any meaningful interactions, capture the event, or request a redraw.

By default, this method does and returns nothing.

### `mouse_interaction`

```rust
fn mouse_interaction( &self, _state: &Self::State, _bounds: Rectangle, _cursor: Cursor, ) -> Interaction
```

Returns the current mouse interaction of the [`Program`](trait.Program.md).

The interaction returned will be in effect even if the cursor position is out of bounds of the program’s [`Canvas`](struct.Canvas.md).

# `iced_widget::checkbox::Status`

```rust
pub enum Status {
    Active {
        is_checked: bool,
    },
    Hovered {
        is_checked: bool,
    },
    Disabled {
        is_checked: bool,
    },
}
```

The possible status of a [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md).

**Source:** [checkbox.rs](../../src/iced_widget/checkbox.rs.md) (lines 519-535)

## Variants

### `Active`

The [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) can be interacted with.

**Fields**

- `is_checked: bool` — Indicates if the [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) is currently checked.

### `Hovered`

The [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) can be interacted with and it is being hovered.

**Fields**

- `is_checked: bool` — Indicates if the [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) is currently checked.

### `Disabled`

The [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) cannot be interacted with.

**Fields**

- `is_checked: bool` — Indicates if the [`Checkbox`](struct.Checkbox.md) is currently checked.

# `iced_widget::checkbox`

Checkboxes can be used to let users make binary choices.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::checkbox;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
}

enum Message {
    CheckboxToggled(bool),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    checkbox(state.is_checked)
        .label("Toggle me!")
        .on_toggle(Message::CheckboxToggled)
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::CheckboxToggled(is_checked) => {
            state.is_checked = is_checked;
        }
    }
}
```

![Checkbox drawn by iced_wgpu](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced/blob/7760618fb112074bc40b148944521f312152012a/docs/images/checkbox.png?raw=true)

# `iced_widget::checkbox::Checkbox`

```rust
pub struct Checkbox<'a, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer> where
```

A box that can be checked.

```rust
use iced::widget::checkbox;

struct State {
   is_checked: bool,
```

# `iced_widget::combo_box`

Combo boxes display a dropdown list of searchable and selectable options.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::combo_box;

struct State {
   fruits: combo_box::State<Fruit>,
   favorite: Option<Fruit>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Orange,
    Strawberry,
    Tomato,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    FruitSelected(Fruit),
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    combo_box(
        &state.fruits,
        "Select your favorite fruit...",
        state.favorite.as_ref(),
        Message::FruitSelected
    )
}

fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
    match message {
        Message::FruitSelected(fruit) => {
            state.favorite = Some(fruit);
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Fruit {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Self::Apple => "Apple",
            Self::Orange => "Orange",
            Self::Strawberry => "Strawberry",
            Self::Tomato => "Tomato",
        })
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`ComboBox`](struct.ComboBox.md) — A widget for searching and selecting a single value from a list of options.
- [`State`](struct.State.md) — The local state of a [`ComboBox`](struct.ComboBox.md).

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`ComboBox`](struct.ComboBox.md).

# `iced_widget::component`

Build and reuse custom widgets using The Elm Architecture.

## Traits

- [`Component`](trait.Component.md) — A reusable, custom widget that uses The Elm Architecture.

## Functions

- [`component`](fn.component.md) — Turns an implementor of [`Component`](trait.Component.md) into an [`Element`] that can be embedded in any application.

# `iced_widget::component::Component`

```rust
pub trait Component<'a, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer> where
    Renderer: Renderer, {
    type State: Default + 'static;
    type Event: 'static;

    // Required methods
    fn update(
        &self,
        state: &mut Self::State,
        event: Self::Event,
        renderer: &Renderer,
    ) -> Option<Message>;
    fn view(
        &self,
        state: &Self::State,
    ) -> impl Widget<Self::Event, Theme, Renderer> + 'a;

    // Provided methods
    fn listen(
        &self,
        _state: &Self::State,
        _event: &Event,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _cursor: Cursor,
    ) -> Action<Self::Event> { ... }
    fn mouse_interaction(&self, _state: &Self::State) -> Interaction { ... }
    fn diff(&mut self, _state: &mut Self::State) { ... }
    fn operate(
        &self,
        _state: &mut Self::State,
        _bounds: Rectangle,
        _operation: &mut dyn Operation,
    ) { ... }
}
```

A reusable, custom widget that uses The Elm Architecture.

A [`Component`](trait.Component.md) allows you to implement custom widgets as if they were `iced` applications with encapsulated state.

In other words, a [`Component`](trait.Component.md) allows you to turn `iced` applications into custom widgets and embed them without cumbersome wiring.

A [`Component`](trait.Component.md) produces widgets that may fire an [`Event`](trait.Component.md) and update the internal state of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

Additionally, a [`Component`](trait.Component.md) is capable of producing a `Message` to notify the parent application of any relevant interactions.

## State

A component can store its state in one of two ways: either as data within the implementor of the trait, or in a type [`State`](trait.Component.md) that is managed by the runtime and provided to the trait methods. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and have opposite pros and cons.

For instance, if a piece of state is needed by multiple components that reside in different branches of the tree, then it’s more convenient to let a common ancestor store it and pass it down.

On the other hand, if a piece of state is only needed by the component itself, you can store it as part of its internal [`State`](trait.Component.md).

**Source:** [component.rs](../../src/iced_widget/component.rs.md) (lines 42-111)

## Required Associated Types

### `State`

```rust
type State: Default + 'static
```

The internal state of this [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

### `Event`

```rust
type Event: 'static
```

The type of event this [`Component`](trait.Component.md) handles internally.

## Required Methods

### `update`

```rust
fn update( &self, state: &mut Self::State, event: Self::Event, renderer: &Renderer, ) -> Option<Message>
```

Processes an [`Event`](trait.Component.md) and updates the [`Component`](trait.Component.md) state accordingly.

It can produce a `Message` for the parent application.

### `view`

```rust
fn view( &self, state: &Self::State, ) -> impl Widget<Self::Event, Theme, Renderer> + 'a
```

Produces the widgets of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md), which may trigger an [`Event`](trait.Component.md) on user interaction.

## Provided Methods

### `listen`

```rust
fn listen( &self, _state: &Self::State, _event: &Event, _bounds: Rectangle, _cursor: Cursor, ) -> Action<Self::Event>
```

Listens to a runtime [`Event`](../canvas/enum.Event.md) and performs an [`Action`](../struct.Action.md) as a result.

If the [`Action`](../struct.Action.md) publishes a [`Component::Event`](trait.Component.md), it will be immediately fed to [`update`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it returns [`Action::none`](../struct.Action.md).

### `mouse_interaction`

```rust
fn mouse_interaction(&self, _state: &Self::State) -> Interaction
```

Returns the current [`mouse::Interaction`] of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

This interaction will override any interaction produced by the [`view`](trait.Component.md) of the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it returns [`mouse::Interaction::None`].

### `diff`

```rust
fn diff(&mut self, _state: &mut Self::State)
```

Reconciles the current [`Component`](trait.Component.md) with its internal [`State`](trait.Component.md) persisted in the widget tree.

This method will be called every time the widget tree changes. You can leverage it to detect and react to changes in the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it does nothing.

### `operate`

```rust
fn operate( &self, _state: &mut Self::State, _bounds: Rectangle, _operation: &mut dyn Operation, )
```

Run the provided [`widget::Operation`] on the [`Component`](trait.Component.md).

By default, it does nothing.

# `iced_widget::container`

Containers let you align a widget inside their boundaries.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::container;

enum Message {
    // ...
}

fn view(state: &State) -> impl Widget<Message> {
    container("This text is centered inside a rounded box!")
        .padding(10)
        .center(800)
        .style(container::rounded_box)
}
```

## Structs

- [`Container`](struct.Container.md) — A widget that aligns its contents inside of its boundaries.
- [`Style`](struct.Style.md) — The appearance of a container.

## Traits

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of a [`Container`](struct.Container.md).

## Functions

- [`background`](fn.background.md) — A [`Container`](struct.Container.md) with the given [`Background`].
- [`bordered_box`](fn.bordered_box.md) — A bordered [`Container`](struct.Container.md) with a background.
- [`danger`](fn.danger.md) — A [`Container`](struct.Container.md) with a danger background color.
- [`dark`](fn.dark.md) — A [`Container`](struct.Container.md) with a dark background and white text.
- [`draw_background`](fn.draw_background.md) — Draws the background of a [`Container`](struct.Container.md) given its [`Style`](struct.Style.md) and its `bounds`.
- [`layout`](fn.layout.md) — Computes the layout of a [`Container`](struct.Container.md).
- [`primary`](fn.primary.md) — A [`Container`](struct.Container.md) with a primary background color.
- [`rounded_box`](fn.rounded_box.md) — A rounded [`Container`](struct.Container.md) with a background.

### `impl<T> IntoEither for T`

# `iced_widget::grid::Sizing`

```rust
pub enum Sizing {
    AspectRatio(f32),
    EvenlyDistribute(Length),
}
```

The sizing strategy of a [`Grid`](struct.Grid.md).

**Source:** [grid.rs](../../src/iced_widget/grid.rs.md) (lines 334-345)

## Variants

### `AspectRatio(f32)`

The [`Grid`](struct.Grid.md) will ensure each cell follows the given aspect ratio and the total size will be the sum of the cells and the spacing between them.

The ratio is the amount of horizontal pixels per each vertical pixel of a cell in the [`Grid`](struct.Grid.md).

### `EvenlyDistribute(Length)`

The [`Grid`](struct.Grid.md) will evenly distribute the space available in the given [`Length`] for each cell.

# `iced_widget::keyed`

Keyed widgets can provide hints to ensure continuity.

## What is continuity?

Continuity is the feeling of persistence of state.

In a graphical user interface, users expect widgets to have a certain degree of continuous state. For instance, a text input that is focused should stay focused even if the widget tree changes slightly.

Continuity is tricky in `iced` and the Elm Architecture because the whole widget tree is rebuilt during every `view` call. This is very convenient from a developer perspective because you can build extremely dynamic interfaces without worrying about changing state.

However, the tradeoff is that determining what changed becomes hard for `iced`. If you have a list of things, adding an element at the top may cause a loss of continuity on every element on the list!

## How can we keep continuity?

The good news is that user interfaces generally have a static widget structure. This structure can be relied on to ensure some degree of continuity. `iced` already does this.

However, sometimes you have a certain part of your interface that is quite dynamic. For instance, a list of things where items may be added or removed at any place.

There are different ways to mitigate this during the reconciliation stage, but they involve comparing trees at certain depths and backtracking… Quite computationally expensive.

One approach that is cheaper consists in letting the user provide some hints about the identities of the different widgets so that they can be compared directly without going deeper.

The widgets in this module will all ask for a “hint” of some sort. In order to help them keep continuity, you need to make sure the hint stays the same for the same items in your user interface between `view` calls.

## Re-exports

- [`Column`](column/struct.Column.md)

## Modules

- [`column`](column/index.md) — Keyed columns distribute content vertically while keeping continuity.

# `iced_widget::markdown::Item`

```rust
pub enum Item {
    Heading(HeadingLevel, Text),
    Paragraph(Text),
    CodeBlock {
        language: Option<String>,
        code: String,
        lines: Vec<Text>,
    },
    List {
        start: Option<u64>,
        bullets: Vec<Bullet>,
    },
    Image {
        url: Uri,
        title: String,
        alt: Text,
    },
    Quote(Vec<Item>),
    Rule,
    Table {
        columns: Vec<Column>,
        rows: Vec<Row>,
    },
}
```

A Markdown item.

**Source:** [markdown.rs](../../src/iced_widget/markdown.rs.md) (lines 730-773)

## Variants

### `Heading(HeadingLevel, Text)`

A heading.

### `Paragraph(Text)`

A paragraph.

### `CodeBlock`

A code block.

You can enable the `highlighter` feature for syntax highlighting.

**Fields**

- `language: Option<String>` — The language of the code block, if any.
- `code: String` — The raw code of the code block.
- `lines: Vec<Text>` — The styled lines of text in the code block.

### `List`

A list.

**Fields**

- `start: Option<u64>` — The first number of the list, if it is ordered.
- `bullets: Vec<Bullet>` — The items of the list.

### `Image`

An image.

**Fields**

- `url: Uri` — The destination URL of the image.
- `title: String` — The title of the image.
- `alt: Text` — The alternative text of the image.

### `Quote(Vec<Item>)`

A quote.

### `Rule`

A horizontal separator.

### `Table`

A table.

**Fields**

- `columns: Vec<Column>` — The columns of the table.
- `rows: Vec<Row>` — The rows of the table.

```rust
fn into_either(self, into_left: bool) -> Either<Self, Self>
```

Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right) variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html) otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either)

#### `into_either_with`

```rust

```

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left) variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html) if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right) variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html) otherwise. # `iced_widget::markdown::parse`

```rust
pub fn parse(markdown: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = Item> + '_
```

Parse the given Markdown content.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::markdown;
use iced::{Theme, Widget};

struct State {
   markdown: Vec<markdown::Item>,
}

enum Message {
    LinkClicked(markdown::Uri),
}

impl State {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            markdown: markdown::parse("This is some **Markdown**!").collect(),
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message> {
        markdown::view(
            &self.markdown,
            markdown::Settings::default(),
            Theme::TokyoNight,
        )
            .map(Message::LinkClicked)
    }

    fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::LinkClicked(url) => {
                println!("The following url was clicked: {url}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# `iced_widget::markdown::sections`

```rust
pub fn sections<'a>(
    items: &'a [Item],
) -> impl Iterator<Item = (Option<&'a Item>, &'a [Item])> + 'a
```

Groups the given Markdown [`Item`](enum.Item.md)s by [`Item::Heading`](enum.Item.md).

The returned iterator yields a `(Option<&Item>, &[Item])` pair for each group, without cloning any [`Item`](enum.Item.md):

- The first element is the heading that starts the group, if any. It is [`None`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) for the group of items that appears before the first heading, if there is any;
- The second element is the slice of items that follow the heading, up to (but not including) the next one.

Every item in the given slice is yielded exactly once: a heading is returned as the first element of the group it starts, and every other item is part of the slice that follows the last heading before it.

## Example

```rust
use iced_widget::markdown;

let items: Vec<_> = markdown::parse("# Title\n\nHello!\n\n# Subtitle\n\nMore!").collect();

let mut groups = markdown::sections(&items);

let (heading, contents) = groups.next().unwrap();
assert!(heading.is_some());
assert_eq!(contents.len(), 1);

let (heading, contents) = groups.next().unwrap();
assert!(heading.is_some());
assert_eq!(contents.len(), 1);

assert!(groups.next().is_none());
```

**Source:** [markdown.rs](../../src/iced_widget/markdown.rs.md) (lines 677-726)

# `iced_widget::markdown`

Markdown widgets can parse and display Markdown.

You can enable the `highlighter` feature for syntax highlighting in code blocks.

Only the variants of [`Item`](enum.Item.md) are currently supported.

## Example

```rust
use iced::widget::markdown;
use iced::{Theme, Widget};

struct State {
   markdown: Vec<markdown::Item>,
}

enum Message {
    LinkClicked(markdown::Uri),
}

impl State {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            markdown: markdown::parse("This is some **Markdown**!").collect(),
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> impl Widget<Message> {
        markdown::view(
            &self.markdown,
            markdown::Settings::default(),
            Theme::TokyoNight,
        )
            .map(Message::LinkClicked)
    }

    fn update(state: &mut State, message: Message) {
        match message {
            Message::LinkClicked(url) => {
                println!("The following url was clicked: {url}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Structs

- [`Column`](struct.Column.md) — The column of a table.
- [`Content`](struct.Content.md) — A bunch of Markdown that has been parsed.
- [`DefaultViewer`](struct.DefaultViewer.md) — The default [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md).
- [`Highlight`](struct.Highlight.md) — A text highlight.
- [`InlineCode`](struct.InlineCode.md) — The style of some inline code.
- [`Row`](struct.Row.md) — The row of a table.
- [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md) — Configuration controlling Markdown rendering in [`view`](../fn.markdown.md).
- [`Text`](struct.Text.md) — A bunch of parsed Markdown text.

- [`Bullet`](enum.Bullet.md) — The item of a list.
- [`HeadingLevel`](enum.HeadingLevel.md)
- [`Item`](enum.Item.md) — A Markdown item.

- [`Catalog`](trait.Catalog.md) — The theme catalog of Markdown items.

- [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) — A view strategy to display a Markdown [`Item`](enum.Item.md).

# `iced_widget::markdown::Content`

```rust
pub struct Content { /* private fields */ }
```

A bunch of Markdown that has been parsed.

**Source:** [markdown.rs](../../src/iced_widget/markdown.rs.md) (lines 79-107)

## Methods

### `impl Content`

#### `new`

```rust
pub fn new() -> Self
```

Creates a new empty [`Content`](struct.Content.md).

#### `parse`

```rust
pub fn parse(markdown: &str) -> Self
```

Creates some new [`Content`](struct.Content.md) by parsing the given Markdown.

#### `push_str`

```rust
pub fn push_str(&mut self, markdown: &str)
```

Pushes more Markdown into the [`Content`](struct.Content.md); parsing incrementally!

This is specially useful when you have long streams of Markdown; like big files or potentially long replies.

Only the last item is re-parsed on every call; and, when the last item is a list, only its last bullet is re-parsed, so that pushing new items to a long list stays cheap.

The result converges to the one obtained by parsing the whole stream at once, as the stream grows.

#### `items`

```rust
pub fn items(&self) -> &[Item]
```

Returns the Markdown items, ready to be rendered.

You can use [`view`](../fn.markdown.md) to turn them into a [`Widget`](../trait.Widget.md).

#### `images`

```rust
pub fn images(&self) -> &HashSet<Uri>
```

Returns the URLs of the Markdown images present in the [`Content`](struct.Content.md).

#### `raw`

```rust
pub fn raw(&self) -> &str
```

Returns the raw Markdown.

## Methods

### `impl Settings`

#### `with_text_size`

```rust
pub fn with_text_size(text_size: impl Into<Pixels>) -> Self
```

Creates new [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md) with the given base text size in [`Pixels`].

Heading levels will be adjusted automatically. Specifically, the first level will be 1.5 times the base size, the second 1.25 times, the third 1.125 times, and the remaining levels will use the base size.

#### `line_height`

```rust
pub fn line_height(self, line_height: impl Into<LineHeight>) -> Self
```

Sets the [`LineHeight`](../text/enum.LineHeight.md) of the [`Settings`](struct.Settings.md).

# `iced_widget::markdown::Viewer`

```rust
pub trait Viewer<'a, Message, Theme = Theme, Renderer = Renderer> where
    Self: Sized + 'a,
    Message: 'a,
    Theme: Catalog + 'a,
    Renderer: Renderer + 'a, {
    // Required methods
    fn theme(&self) -> &Theme;
    fn highlighter(&self) -> &dyn Highlighter<Code, Theme>;
    fn on_link_click(url: Uri) -> Message;

    // Provided methods
    fn image(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        url: &'a Uri,
        title: &'a str,
        alt: &Text,
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn heading(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        level: &'a HeadingLevel,
        text: &'a Text,
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn paragraph(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        text: &Text,
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn code_block(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        language: Option<&'a str>,
        code: &'a str,
        lines: &'a [Text],
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn unordered_list(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        bullets: &'a [Bullet],
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn ordered_list(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        start: u64,
        bullets: &'a [Bullet],
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn quote(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        contents: &'a [Item],
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn rule(&self) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
    fn table(
        &self,
        settings: Settings,
        columns: &'a [Column],
        rows: &'a [Row],
    ) -> impl Widget<Message, Theme, Renderer> + 'a { ... }
}
```

A view strategy to display a Markdown [`Item`](enum.Item.md).

A [`Viewer`](trait.Viewer.md) is in charge of turning each [`Item`](enum.Item.md) into a widget. It also provides the [`Theme`](../enum.Theme.md) and [`text::Highlighter`](../text/trait.Highlighter.md) used for rendering.
